adapter.name: stanag4609
adapter.why_the_two_names_differ: The adapter takes the STANAG's number because STANAG 4609 is, in MISP-2019.1 SS C.1.2's own words, 'a covering document rather than a standalone document, which points directly to a version of the U.S. Motion Imagery Standards Profile (MISP)' - so there is no NATO document whose CONTENT could name the adapter, while the STANAG number is what an ICD, a NISP row and a national ratification record all call the feed. The fixture directory takes the content's name because a directory holds PAYLOADS and a payload is not a standard, which is the same split that puts adapter stanag4676's fixtures in fixtures/nits. The adapter-shaped content is the KLV metadata stream, so the directory is klv and the payload extension will be .klv.

rejected_directory_names.misp: Names the governing profile, which is a DOCUMENT - the pinned PDF would sit at fixtures/misp/spec/misb-misp-2019-1.pdf, a directory named after a file inside it. It also names the wrong layer: the MISP governs the imagery, the audio, the containers and the transport as well, and this adapter reads one of the five.
rejected_directory_names.misb: Names the publisher. fixtures/eurocontrol would have been wrong for CAT048 for the same reason.
rejected_directory_names.fmv: Rejected by the pinned text itself, MISP SS 2.1.1: 'FMV has no formal definition and conveys different meanings to different communities; therefore, the term FMV should not be used in any contractual language.' A fixture directory name is closer to contractual language than to prose.
rejected_directory_names.stanag4609: Would reproduce the bug commit 80b38d1 had to fix - three NITS PDFs sitting in a directory named for the adapter because a copy command took the adapter's name where the fixture directory's name was wanted.

the_normative_act.aim: The aim of this NATO standardization agreement (STANAG) is to respond to the following interoperability requirements.
the_normative_act.interoperability_requirement: To provide common methods for the generation, dissemination, exploitation and archive of Motion Imagery (MI) among National and NATO Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) systems.
the_normative_act.agreement: Participating nations agree to implement the following standard.
the_normative_act.standard: U.S. Motion Imagery Standards Board (MISB) Motion Imagery Standards Profile-2019.1 (MISP-2019.1)
the_normative_act.other_related_documents: U.S. Motion Imagery Standards Board (MISB) Motion Imagery Standards Profile-2019.1 (MISP-2019.1): Motion Imagery Handbook
the_normative_act.implementation_of_the_agreement: MISP-2019.1 defines the technical requirements for motion imagery formats, compression, metadata and transmission protocols for ISR systems and systems that manage and/or exploit motion imagery data.
the_normative_act.what_it_contains_that_is_technical: Nothing. The wrapper states no field, no encoding, no layout and no requirement of its own. Every technical requirement this adapter could implement is in the profile it promulgates, which is why there are two pins and not one.

delegated_specifications_held.what_this_is: The delegated documents this repository holds on disk. MISP-2019.1 delegates every field dictionary it relies on to a document published by somebody else, AND NOT EVERY DOCUMENT IT DELEGATES TO IS ONE, which is why this sentence says documents. Fourteen delegations are in scope: THIRTEEN are named in delegation_table below, and the fourteenth is the MISP-2019.1 Motion Imagery Handbook, park 10, which the WRAPPER names under OTHER RELATED DOCUMENTS and delegation_table does not carry. EIGHT of the fourteen are here - ST 0601.14, ST 0102.12, ST 0107.3, ST 1402.2, ST 1201.3, ST 1303.1, ST 1204.1 and ST 1301.2 - and this node holds TEN documents, because ST 0601.19 and EG 0601.1 are held and are not delegations. A document this repository holds and a delegation the profile makes are different things, and the tally counts the second. ST 0102.12 and ST 0601.14 are the exact editions the profile pins. ST 0601.19 is NOT - it is five major revisions later than the 0601.14 ref [53] cites - and it is retained as CONTEXT ONLY under reconciliation_ruling.ruling_st_0601: useful for the item-42 divergence note and for knowing where the standard went, and never a source of tag semantics for this row set. CORRECTED 2026-08-28 BY THE RULED ROUND, AND EVERY PART OF THE CORRECTION WAS ALREADY RULED ELSEWHERE IN THIS RECORD - nothing here is a new judgment about what a field dictionary is. (1) THE TERM. The opening read field dictionaries. The length round ruled that term wrong for this set on 2026-08-26, when ST 0107.3 arrived and the top-level header recorded it as the first one here that is not a field dictionary - six pages of KLV-wide baseline requirements - which is why field dictionaries became documents in THAT sentence. FORMAT_COVERAGE.md says the same in its own words at its tally row. The repair was made at two sites on the day it was ruled and was not made at this one. (2) THE COUNT. It read THREE and never moved. It was written at commit 642280b over a node that held exactly three documents - ST 0601.14, ST 0102.12 and ST 0601.19 - so it was right as a count of what was HERE that day and was ALREADY ONE TOO HIGH as a count of delegations, because the ST 0601.19 copy is retained as context only. That is the same off-by-one the repair round annotated in the top-level header opening and the decay sweep repaired in FORMAT_COVERAGE.md, and THIS IS ITS THIRD SITE - the first where the figure and the term were wrong together. The node then reached four, six and ten documents and the delegations reached three, four and eight; the sentence passed through a point where THREE was accidentally right as a delegation count and wrong as a held count, which is the reading that kept it alive. (3) THE LOCUS. Fourteen is the right total and delegation_table is the wrong place to send a reader for all of it: that node names thirteen, and the fourteenth is the Handbook the wrapper names. THE REASON IS RESTORED WITH THE FIGURE AND NOT THE FIGURE ALONE, on the precedent the delegated-document tally repair set at 646b306: the reason is what got dropped when the count became arithmetic, and a figure standing with no reason beside it is the one that goes stale in silence.

provenance_ruling.page_as_source: The source of record for a MISB standard is its NSG Registry document page - https://nsgreg.nga.mil/doc/view?i=<n> - and not the URL the bytes arrived over. The page is stable, dereferenceable and states the registry's own view of the document's identity: its version, its registration status and what it supersedes.
provenance_ruling.hash_as_copy: The SHA-256 identifies the COPY THAT WAS READ, which is a different claim from the edition number. This is house style in every pin record here and this round is the first to prove why it is not pedantry: ST 0601.19's cover says 02 March 2023 and the copy on disk carries two amendment rows dated after that, under the same edition number and with no minor-version letter on the cover. The edition number cannot distinguish those two documents. The hash can.
provenance_ruling.why_download_urls_are_not_recorded: The registry serves documents over EPHEMERAL PRESIGNED LINKS. Such a URL expires, so recording one would put a dead string in the source field of a record whose whole purpose is to be checkable years later. The doc/view page is what a reader is sent to; the presigned link is a transport detail of one retrieval.
provenance_ruling.what_the_edition_date_field_means: The date the DOCUMENT states for itself, read off its own cover or front matter, and authoritative for this field where the document states one. Where the registry page states a date too, both are recorded and required to agree - see st_0102_12 below, where three independent statements of 22 June 2017 agree.
provenance_ruling.the_registry_pages_were_not_machine_veri: HONEST LIMIT ON THE SOURCE FIELD. Both doc/view URLs are recorded as the citable source and neither was retrieved by this round: nsgreg.nga.mil answers an automated GET with a CAPTCHA interstitial, so the page's stated version, registration status and supersession line could not be read mechanically. They are recorded as reported. Every fact this round ASSERTS about either document - hash, byte count, page count, edition date, title-page identity - was taken from the bytes on disk instead, which is the stronger source for those five and the reason the ruling below does not rest on the registry at all. The parks' reopen route is unaffected: a CAPTCHA is a bot gate, not an account gate, and a person with a browser is not blocked.

st_0601_14.document: MISB ST 0601.14, UAS Datalink Local Set
st_0601_14.edition_as_the_profile_cites_it: 'MISB ST 0601.14 UAS Datalink Local Set, Nov 2018' - MISP-2019.1 Appendix B reference [53], verbatim, and the 2019.1 Change Log agrees. The citation carries NO minor-version letter, which is the whole subject of the_copy_is_the_a_minor_revision below.
st_0601_14.registry_page_as_reported: Read from the document's page by the operator and recorded as reported, on the same footing as the two registry pages already in this record - see provenance_ruling.the_registry_pages_were_not_machine_verified_and_why, which still holds: nsgreg.nga.mil answers an automated GET with a CAPTCHA interstitial. Document ID 4739. Edition 'Version 1.14'. Edition date 01 November 2018. Status SUPERSEDED, 6 Jun 2019. Superseded by document 4803 (ST 0601.15). Supersedes document 4679 (ST 0601.13). Every fact this round ASSERTS about the copy - hash, byte count, page count, cover identity, cover date, revision history, tag table - was taken from the bytes on disk instead.
st_0601_14.superseded_is_not_withdrawn: EXPECTED AND ACCEPTABLE, and recorded so that nobody re-opens it as a defect. The profile froze its references in November 2018 and the registry moved on: ST 0601.14 was superseded on 6 June 2019 by 0601.15 and has been superseded four more times since. A profile that pins a revision pins the document that revision names, and that document does not stop being the pinned one when a later revision is registered - it stops being the CURRENT one. This is why parks.shared_exit_condition says 'obtain the EXACT version the delegation table pins (not the current one)'. Superseded entries stay registered and stay downloadable, which is what made this round possible; a WITHDRAWN entry would be a different fact and this one is not withdrawn.
st_0601_14.the_copy_is_the_a_minor_revision: THE KLV 9 HAZARD ARRIVING AT FETCH TIME RATHER THAN BEING FOUND LATER, and the reason this field exists before any tag was read. The registry serves this edition as ST0601.14a.pdf - a single-letter Minor Version that the citation 'MISB ST 0601.14' does not carry and cannot carry. THE FILENAME IS KEPT AS THE REGISTRY SERVES IT, deliberately and not as an oversight: the FILENAME states the copy, the `edition` field states the edition the profile cites ('0601.14'), and the SHA-256 states the identity. Renaming the file to ST0601.14.pdf would make the directory listing agree with the citation by destroying the one piece of evidence that they differ. Cross-reference ambiguity_register KLV 9, which is the same coming-apart discovered in ST 0601.19 by a check nobody asked for, and KLV 10, which is this one.
st_0601_14.what_the_document_itself_says_about_the_: READ FROM THE PDF's OWN COVER AND REVISION HISTORY rather than inferred from the filename. (1) The cover prints 'MISB ST 0601.14a' - the letter is on the document, not only on the file. (2) Section 2 states the convention: 'In the event of a MISB document correction, the corrected document will have a single letter Minor Version appended to the Major Version number per the MISB Document Development Process [1]. For example, corrections to ST 0001.2, which has a Major Version of 2, result in a new version titled ST 0001.2a, which includes a Minor Version of "a". The MISB will not update the referring document (this document) with the Minor Version number change. When acquiring any MISB reference listed below from an NGA repository the latest version may be either a Major or Minor Version.' So the profile's failure to cite the 'a' is not an error in the profile - it is the convention working as written. (3) The revision history table on PDF page 3 says what the 'a' CHANGED, in one line: 'ST 0601.14a | 05/1/2020 | Corrected table headers in Item 47 - Generic Flags.' One corrected table header, in one item, in a 218-page document.
st_0601_14.edition_date_read_from: The document's own cover, which prints 'MISB ST 0601.14a' and '1 May 2020', and the footer of all 218 pages, which repeats '1 May 2020'. Per provenance_ruling.what_the_edition_date_field_means - the date the DOCUMENT states for itself, authoritative for this field where the document states one - this field is 1 May 2020. IT IS THE DATE OF THE 'a' MINOR REVISION AND NOT OF EDITION .14, and the next field is why that is a distinction and not a contradiction.
st_0601_14.the_two_dates_are_two_different_facts_an: NOT A CONTRADICTION, and it was checked as one before it was recorded as a distinction. The registry reports edition date 01 November 2018 for Version 1.14; the cover of this copy says 1 May 2020. Those date different things, and THE DOCUMENT ITSELF SAYS SO: its revision history table opens with the row 'ST 0601.14 | 11/1/2018' - 1 November 2018, in the MM/D/YYYY form this publisher uses throughout - and then adds 'ST 0601.14a | 05/1/2020'. So the document, the registry page and MISP-2019.1 Appendix B reference [53]'s 'Nov 2018' all agree on when edition .14 was issued, and the cover date belongs to the correction. Had the document's own revision history NOT carried the 11/1/2018 row, this round would have stopped and reported a contradiction between the fetched document and the registry facts it was briefed with; it carries it, so this is a distinction.
st_0601_14.this_is_the_edition_the_profile_pins: YES, and it is what re-opened Act 3. MISP-2019.1 Appendix B reference [53] reads 'MISB ST 0601.14 UAS Datalink Local Set, Nov 2018'; this document's revision history dates edition .14 to 11/1/2018 and its cover carries the .14 major version. The minor-version letter does not change which edition this is - section 2 says a Minor Version is a CORRECTION to the Major Version and that referring documents are not updated for it - so this copy is the 0601.14 the profile pins, corrected once. See reconciliation_ruling.ruling_st_0601.
st_0601_14.the_copy_is_not_the_pristine_1_may_2020_: THE SAME FINDING AS ST 0601.19's, ONE TURN WORSE, and again it was not looked for. The revision history table on PDF page 3 carries a THIRD row, dated 08/19/2021, with four editorial bullets - normalising the item 12 example, clarifying Offset Corner items 26 thru 33, fixing the item 131 example to use 7 bytes, and 'Miscellaneous editorial changes'. ITS REVISION CELL IS EMPTY. That was checked positionally and not read off a text dump: in the page's own drawn grid the Revision column runs from x=75.4 to x=98.4, the '.14a' row places 'ST 0601.1'/'4'/'a' at x=75.9-129.2, and the 08/19/2021 row places nothing in that column at all - its leftmost item is the date at x=146.2. The file's own /CreationDate is D:20211217145743-05'00', 17 December 2021, after that row. So this copy is ST 0601.14a as further amended through 19 August 2021, generated 17 December 2021, wearing a 1 May 2020 cover and a version number that names neither amendment. ST 0601.19's cover at least kept a stable edition number over its two undeclared amendments; here the amendment is not even given a letter, so there is no string ANY citation could use to name it. The SHA-256 is. Recorded as ambiguity KLV 10.

eg_0601_1.the_document_is_an_EG_AND_NOT_AN_ST_AND_: THERE IS NO 'MISB ST 0601.1'. Park 13 was opened under the name 'MISB ST 0601.1', which is a document that was never published, and the name was not this repository's invention: ST 0601.14a SS 8.65 defines item 65's value range as '1..255 corresponds to document revisions MISB ST 0601.1 thru MISB ST 0601.255', projecting the current series name back onto twelve editions that carried a different one. Edition 1's own SS 7.65 states the same range as 'EG0601.1 thru EG0601.255'. So a reader following SS 8.65 to the letter is sent to a document that does not exist, and this pin is the document SS 8.65's '0601.1' DENOTES. Registered as KLV 15.

delegated_specifications_held.the_document_information_dictionary_METH: A METHOD THIS RECORD USES, RE-CALIBRATED ON FOUR NEW SAMPLES, AND IT IS WEAKER THAN IT LOOKED. The adjudication round introduced the PDF document-information dictionary as the 'cheapest useful read in the set' and calibrated it on the four held 0601 documents, where /CreationDate equalled the cover date exactly for three and post-dated it by four days for the initial release. ST 1402.2 then post-dated by 47 days. THE FOUR DOCUMENTS PINNED ON 2026-08-27 EVENING POST-DATE THEIR COVERS BY 462, 63, 47 AND 288 DAYS. So across the nine samples now held the delta runs 0 to 462 days and the field corroborates only that a file was PRODUCED NO EARLIER THAN its cover date. AT 462 DAYS IT DOES NOT CORROBORATE EVEN THE YEAR, which is exactly the claim st_1402_2's node makes for it ('corroborates the YEAR and nothing finer') - so that sentence is true of that document and is NOT true as a general rule, and it is narrowed here rather than edited there, on entry 5's rule that a closed record which quietly updates its own history is a record nobody can date. WHAT THE FIELD IS STILL GOOD FOR: a LOWER bound, and detecting a file re-saved long after its cover - which is itself the KLV 9 / KLV 10 hazard seen from the file side rather than the page side. What it is NOT good for is corroborating a cover date, which is what it was first used to do. AMENDED 2026-08-28 BY THE REPAIR ROUND, AND THE AMENDMENT IS ABOUT COVERAGE RATHER THAN CORRECTNESS. Everything above re-derived from the held bytes today and all nine sampled lags match this record exactly - 0 for EG 0601.1, 4 for the 0601 initial release, 0 for ST 0601.4, 0 for ST 0601.8, 47 for ST 1402.2, 462 for ST 1201.3, 63 for ST 1303.1, 47 for ST 1204.1 and 288 for ST 1301.2. WHAT WAS MISSING IS THE SENTENCE SAYING WHAT THE SAMPLE COVERS. It is NINE OF THIRTEEN, and the thirteen are the held MISB documents that carry a DAY-PRECISION cover date - fifteen PDFs sit in this directory and two of them are not in that set: the NATO STANAG 4609 Edition 5 wrapper is not a MISB document, and MISP-2019.1's cover states 'November 2018', a month with no day, so no lag in days exists to measure for it. THE FOUR UNSAMPLED SPLIT TWO AND TWO. Two are EXCLUDED FOR CAUSE and their lags are not evidence about production delay: ST 0601.19 at 853 days and ST 0601.14a at 595 are the KLV 9 and KLV 10 copies, whose covers are known not to describe their contents, so what their lag measures is an undeclared amendment. The other two are CLEAN AND WERE SIMPLY NEVER SAMPLED - ST 0107.3 at 63 days, and ST 0102.12 at 567. ST 0102.12 IS THE SHARPEST CASE IN THE WHOLE SET AND IT WAS THE ONE LEFT OUT: its cover date is the one this record says three independent statements agree on and it carries a single revision-history row, so it is the least ambiguous document here and it post-dates its own cover by more than any sampled document does. THE WIDEST LAG OVER CLEANLY-DATED COPIES IS THEREFORE 567 DAYS AND NOT 462, and if the NATO wrapper is admitted it is 617. The conclusion above is UNCHANGED IN DIRECTION AND STRENGTHENED IN DEGREE: the field establishes that a file was produced no earlier than its cover and nothing else, it is a lower bound and a detector of late re-saves, and it is not evidence for a cover date. This clause is appended rather than folded into the paragraph above it, on the same entry-5 rule that governs the rest of this record: a closed record which quietly updates its own history is a record nobody can date.

reconciliation_ruling.what_this_is: THE RULING THAT GATES THE TAG TABLES, and it had to exist before any tag table was transcribed, because it is what decides which tag table is authoritative. The question: MISP-2019.1 is the profile STANAG 4609 Edition 5 promulgates, and it pins specific revisions of the documents it delegates to. Do the copies this round obtained match the revisions the profile pins? One ruling per document, and the answers differ.
reconciliation_ruling.method: MISP-2019.1's normative reference list is its Appendix B, PDF pages 63-66. It was read in full and its entries numbered by position, because the profile cites references by bracketed number and the extraction drops the brackets. The numbering was validated rather than assumed: parsed positionally it yields 103 entries, which is the count this record already stated from an earlier reading, and it places all sixteen reference numbers this record asserts elsewhere - [1], [13], [14], [48], [53], [54], [55], [56], [57], [59], [65], [70], [72], [73], [75], [76] - on the documents this record already attributes to them. One Appendix B entry omits its terminal full stop (the ITU-T H.265 (V5) entry, which runs into the ISO/IEC 14496-10 entry after it); that is the document's, it shifted the naive count by one, and it is recorded because it is the only reason the first parse disagreed.

ruling_st_0601.ruling: MISMATCH, and option (b): THE CITED EDITION IS REQUIRED. RESOLVED 2026-08-26 - the cited edition was fetched. See resolution_2026_08_26 below, which is the operative ruling now; the fields above it are the stop that produced the fetch and are kept because a ruling whose grounds are deleted once it is discharged cannot be audited.
grounds: THE REPOSITORY HAS ALREADY RULED THIS, and consistency is not optional. This record's parks.shared_exit_condition, written in an earlier round and covering parks 1-7 and 9-12, reads: 'obtain the EXACT version the delegation table pins (not "the current one" - the profile pins a revision and a later revision is a different document)'. ST 0601 is park 1. Reading 0601.19 against the profile would overturn a standing ruling in passing, which is the failure mode this record's correction_2026_08_25 field exists to record an instance of.

FORMAT_COVERAGE.md's park 1 row already states the hazard in its own words: 'Version .14 specifically: ST 0601 has revisions on both sides of it, and a tag added in a later revision decoded against an earlier one is a plausible number in the wrong field.' That is not a new argument produced to justify a stop; it is the argument the park was opened with.

OPTION (a) IS NOT COMPLETABLE FROM THE COPY IN HAND, which is the decisive practical ground. Option (a) requires recording 'whether any [tags] were added or changed meaning after the cited edition'. ST 0601.19's Table 1 has columns Tag, Name, Units, Format, Len, SDCC, MUL and Description - there is NO column stating which revision introduced an item - and its revision history table carries rows for .19 and its two later amendments and NO rows for .15, .16, .17 or .18. So for any given tag, 'did this exist in .14' cannot be answered from 0601.19 alone. Ruling (a) would mean asserting a delta this round cannot compute.

AND THE HAZARD IS DEMONSTRATED, not hypothetical. 0601.19's revision history records 'Resolved item 42 ambiguity (i.e., MSL or HAE)' on 06/11/2025 - a change to what a tag MEANS, on the mean-sea-level-versus-height-above-ellipsoid axis, which is exactly the class of change that yields a plausible number in the wrong field. It also records 'Added Item 143 - Metadata Substream ID (MSID)' for .19 itself. One documented semantic change and one documented addition, inside the only revision window the document describes.
ruling_st_0601.what_the_document_does_let_us_bound: Recorded because it is real and because it is what a later round would start from, NOT as a basis for proceeding. ST 0601 stamps each requirement with the version that introduced it, so the post-.14 REQUIREMENT delta is enumerable from 0601.19 alone: twelve requirements, being ST 0601.15-36, ST 0601.17-37 through ST 0601.17-40, and ST 0601.19-41 through ST 0601.19-47. No requirement names .16 or .18. Appendix A additionally lists retired requirements with the version each came from, including five at ST 0601.14. This bounds the REQUIREMENT delta; it does not bound the ITEM delta, and the item delta is the one a tag table would need.

ruling_stanag_4609_edition_5.question: What does the wrapper itself cite for ST 0601 and ST 0102, and does it agree with MISP-2019.1?
ruling_stanag_4609_edition_5.grounds: STANAG 4609 Edition 5 is five pages and its normative content is read in full. Its AGREEMENT clause reads 'Participating nations agree to implement the following standard' and its STANDARD clause names exactly one document: 'U.S. Motion Imagery Standards Board (MISB) Motion Imagery Standards Profile-2019.1 (MISP-2019.1)'. Its OTHER RELATED DOCUMENTS clause names one more, the MISP-2019.1 Motion Imagery Handbook. The strings '0601' and '0102' do not occur in the document at all. It has no reference list of its own.
ruling_stanag_4609_edition_5.ruling: NO CONFLICT TO RECONCILE, and this is a finding rather than an absence of one. The wrapper cites no edition of either document, so it cannot agree or disagree with MISP-2019.1 about one. It delegates the entire question, which makes MISP-2019.1 the SOLE authority for what edition of ST 0601 and ST 0102 governs a STANAG 4609 Edition 5 feed. The two rulings above are therefore the whole of the reconciliation; there is no third opinion to weigh.
ruling_stanag_4609_edition_5.consistent_with_what_this_record_already: wrapper.the_normative_act.what_it_contains_that_is_technical already reads 'Nothing. The wrapper states no field, no encoding, no layout and no requirement of its own.' This round asked a narrower question of the same five pages and got the same answer, which is a corroboration and not a new claim.
ruling_stanag_4609_edition_5.the_one_edition_disagreement_the_wrapper: Not about ST 0601 or ST 0102, and already recorded as ambiguity KLV 3: the wrapper is Edition 5 and MISP-2019.1's Appendix B reference [1] cites 'NATO STANAG 4609: NATO Digital Motion Imagery Standard, Edition 4, 19 Dec 2016' - the profile refers to the edition before the one that promulgates it. Re-read and confirmed verbatim this round.

tag_table_st_0601_14.what_this_is: MISB ST 0601.14's Table 1, 'UAS Datalink Local Set', transcribed in full. This is the field dictionary of the airborne UAS collection - the thing MISP-2019.1 SS 4.4.4.1 delegates and names without describing, and the reason park 1 was the largest park in this section. The Tag, Name, Units, Format, Len and CDM-field columns of FORMAT_COVERAGE.md's ST 0601 row set are generated from `items` below, so those cannot disagree; that row set's Notes column additionally carries this round's per-item findings, which are prose and live there.
tag_table_st_0601_14.source: ST 0601.14a, Table 1, PDF pages 13-17. The copy pinned at delegated_specifications_held.st_0601_14.
tag_table_st_0601_14.the_edition_this_is_read_from: ST 0601.14 and NOT ST 0601.19. ST 0601.14 - this copy, this hash - is the authoritative tag table for this row set; ST 0601.19 remains pinned as context only and is never a source of tag semantics here. Ruled at reconciliation_ruling.ruling_st_0601.resolution_2026_08_26.
tag_table_st_0601_14.how_it_was_transcribed: BY THE TABLE'S OWN DRAWN GRID, not by reading lines off a text dump, and the difference is not cosmetic. Table 1's Description cells wrap to two and three lines and are vertically CENTRED in their row, so a description line frequently sits above the line carrying its own Tag number and below the previous row's. A reader-order text extraction therefore attaches the tail of item 1's description to item 2 - which it did, on the first attempt, silently and plausibly. The transcription instead reads the page's vector rectangles: the column boundaries are the table's own vertical rules, at x = 75.4, 98.4, 217.3, 243.2, 274.2, 292.2, 317.4, 339.0 and 536.4 on every one of the five pages, and the row boundaries are the horizontal cell borders drawn in the Tag column. Each text item is then assigned to the cell its own (x, y) falls in. A cell is what the document draws, so that is what is read.
tag_table_st_0601_14.cross_check_that_makes_the_transcription: THE DOCUMENT STATES THE SAME MAPPING TWICE AND BOTH WERE READ. Table 2, 'Tags Sorted by Name' (PDF pages 17-18), is the same 141 items in alphabetical order across three name/tag column pairs - a completely different grid, extracted by the same method and independently. The two agree on all 141 tag-to-name pairs: no tag in one and not the other, and no name disagreement. Additionally the tag numbers run 1 through 141 with no gap and no duplicate, which is the positive control a summary table can offer about itself.
tag_table_st_0601_14.columns_as_the_document_defines_them: Tag, Name, Units, Format, Len, SDCC, MUL, Description - and the document defines four of them in prose immediately above the table. Units: 'None' means the value is not a measurement, 'Set' or 'Pack' means the value is a collection, 'All other Units are SI enumerations'. Format: 'the item's KLV format for the Value'. Length: 'the nominal length of the value. This may be a required length or variable length' - which is what 'V' means in the length column here. SDCC: whether the item may appear in a Standard Deviation Correlation Coefficient Floating Length Pack, whose own layout is MISB ST 1010.3's. MUL: whether the item may have multiple instances in one Local Set instance.
tag_table_st_0601_14.the_one_note_the_document_attaches_to_th: Quoted because it is a trap and the document says so itself: 'Several Local Set items have the same UL Key but differ in its Type. For example, Tag 22-Target Width, uses a Type of uint16, and Tag 96-Target Width Extended, uses a Type of IMAPB. The Key for both, which is the same, has a MISB ST 0807 dictionary data type of "float". This is an allowed practice, where this document specifies (or overrides) the metadata item's format within the dictionary.' So a decoder keyed on the 16-byte Universal Label alone cannot tell tag 22 from tag 96, and the LOCAL SET TAG is the discriminator. Recorded here rather than in a row, because it is a property of the table.

what_changed_between_14_and_19.what_this_is: MEASURED, from both documents, now that both are in hand - and recorded as a NOTE and never as a source. Not one value in the 141 rows above comes from .19. This node exists so that a reader can see exactly how large the hazard park 1 was opened on turned out to be, and so that the next round to move to a later edition knows what it is moving.
what_changed_between_14_and_19.items_added_in_19: Two: 142 View Domain, and 143 Metadata Substream ID Pack.
what_changed_between_14_and_19.items_removed_in_19: None. All 141 items of .14 survive into .19 at the same tag numbers.
what_changed_between_14_and_19.items_renamed: One: tag 72, 'Event Start Time - UTC' in .14, 'Event Start Time' in .19.
what_changed_between_14_and_19.structural_columns: IDENTICAL on all 141 shared items - Units, Format, Len, SDCC and MUL agree everywhere. This is the reassuring half and it should be read carefully: it means the wire FORM of every .14 item is unchanged in .19, so a .19 stream decoded against this table would not produce a wrong-length read on any shared item. It does not mean the meanings are unchanged.
what_changed_between_14_and_19.descriptions_changed_in_table_1: Eight of 141, and seven are editorial - a comma after 'e.g.', 'Galaleo' corrected to 'Galileo', 'takeoff' to 'take-off', 'Tag' to 'Item' in the cross-references at 137 and 139, and two shortened phrasings at 45 and 126. The eighth, item 136 Leap Seconds, is a real clarification: '.14: Number of leap seconds to adjust Precision Time Stamp (Tag 2) to UTC' against '.19: Number of leap seconds since MISP Epoch to use when converting Precision Time Stamp (Item 2) to UTC'.
what_changed_between_14_and_19.AND THE ONE THAT MATTERS IS NOT IN THAT: ITEM 42's SUMMARY ROW IS BYTE-FOR-BYTE IDENTICAL IN .14 AND .19. Both read 'Calculated target elevation'. The MSL-versus-HAE resolution that .19's revision history announces - 'Resolved item 42 ambiguity (i.e., MSL or HAE)', 06/11/2025 - lives ENTIRELY in the per-item detail section SS 8.42, where .19 adds 'conditionally either MSL or HAE' to the description line, a bullet reading 'Depending on items 25 and/or 78, the measurement base is either MSL or HAE', and three paragraphs of rules keyed on whether items 25 and 78 are present. THIS IS THE FINDING OF THE COMPARISON: a tag table transcribed from Table 1 alone is blind to the single documented semantic change in the whole window. Table 1 is a summary and the per-item sections are the specification, and this round can only say that because it read both.
what_changed_between_14_and_19.what_the_row_set_does_with_it: Records .14's semantics as normative and the divergence as a note, which is what item 42's row does. .14's SS 8.42 states a range, a mapping, a resolution and a recommendation, and states NO datum. So the .14 semantics ARE 'elevation, datum unstated', and that is what the row carries. Importing .19's resolution would be reading the row set against a document this ruling excludes, and it would be doing so at the one item where the two documents actually differ.

what_ST_0601_14_settles_that_the_profile.why_this_node_exists: A CORRECTION TO THE REACH OF TWO EARLIER FINDINGS, and it was found by reading item 2's own section rather than by being looked for. Settlement 3 and register entry KLV 6 are both about what MISP-2019.1 does NOT state, and both are still exactly true about MISP-2019.1. What this round can now add is that the delegated dictionary states it, and the whole discipline of this section is the difference between 'the pinned documents do not say' and 'nobody has read the document that says'.
what_ST_0601_14_settles_that_the_profile.the_epoch_IS_stated_here_and_it_is_state: SS 6.4, verbatim: 'Every UAS Datalink LS packet is required to include a Precision Time Stamp representing absolute time as defined in MISB ST 0603 [4]. The Precision Time Stamp (Tag 2) is an eight-byte unsigned integer counter of the number of SI Seconds (in microseconds) which have elapsed since midnight (00:00:00), January 1, 1970 (1970-01-01T00:00:00Z). Note: this time does not include leap seconds and therefore the Precision Time Stamp does not represent UTC.' SS 8.2 states it again in its own bullet and again in its Details paragraph. So epoch, unit, resolution and leap-second treatment are all read from a pinned document.
what_ST_0601_14_settles_that_the_profile.what_this_corrects_in_settlement_3: NOT THE FINDING - THE REACH. Settlement 3's evidence stands unaltered: `epoch`, `1970`, `microsecond` and `leap` occur zero times in MISP-2019.1's 73 pages, and the premise that the PROFILE fixes the epoch was and is false. What changes is the consequence drawn from it. The old consequence was that this repository could not state the epoch at all without writing down something it had not read. It has now read it, in the document the profile delegates to, and the value is stated with both loci. The rule was never 'do not write an epoch'; it was 'do not write one from memory', and that rule is what allows this.
what_ST_0601_14_settles_that_the_profile.what_this_corrects_in_KLV_6: KLV 6 says nothing in the profile requires a standalone metadata stream to carry an absolute time, resting on the circularity of a requirement that is 'mandatory for Metadata packets which include a Metadata item for a timestamp'. Still true of the profile. ST 0601.14 closes it from the other side for THIS local set and only for this one: SS 6.4 requires the Precision Time Stamp in every UAS Datalink LS packet, Table 1 and SS 8.2 mark item 2 Mandatory, and item 65 is Mandatory with it. A conformant UAS Datalink LS packet therefore always carries an absolute time. That is a fact about ST 0601.14's local set, not about KLV streams in general, and KLV 6 stays in the register because the general claim is the one it makes.
what_ST_0601_14_settles_that_the_profile.what_it_does_NOT_settle_and_why_park_3_s: Three things. FIRST, ST 0603.5 remains the normative definition - SS 6.4 says the Precision Time Stamp represents absolute time 'as defined in MISB ST 0603 [4]' and ST 0601.14 is restating it, so a conflict between the two is resolved by a document not held. SECOND, items 136 (Leap Seconds) and 137 (Correction Offset) exist precisely to convert this scale to UTC and their own semantics are ST 0603's - and .19 later rewrote item 136's summary line to name a 'MISP Epoch', a term ST 0601.14 does not use. THIRD, what to CALL a count of SI seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z that excludes leap seconds is exactly the TAI-versus-UTC question park 3's row says it decides, and ST 0601.14 answers only the negative half: not UTC. So the row for item 2 can now state its epoch, and park 3 stays open.
what_ST_0601_14_settles_that_the_profile.the_reference_agrees_with_the_profile_wh: ST 0601.14's own reference [4] reads 'MISB ST 0603.5 MISP Time System and Timestamps, Oct 2017' - the same revision MISP-2019.1's Appendix B pins for park 3, and the same date. Two independently-pinned documents naming the same revision of a third is the corroboration delegation_table.entries was built to make checkable, and this is the first time it has been available from both sides.

framing_ruling_st_0601_14.what_this_is: THE FRAMING RULING, 2026-08-26. Parks 4 and 8 own how a key, a tag and a length are written, and this round asked the pinned copy of ST 0601.14 whether it states those rules itself. It states two of the three and delegates the third, so this node records each rule as ESTABLISHED with its section, or as UNDERIVABLE with the sentence that delegates it - and parks 4 and 8 both STAY OPEN. Nothing here flips a tag_table_st_0601_14 row: all 141 remain 'not yet', because a framing layer says where an item begins and never what it means.
framing_ruling_st_0601_14.the_document_rule_this_round_worked_unde: Where ST 0601.14a's own text and worked examples state a rule completely enough to implement and test against, the rule is recorded as established from the pinned copy with its sections cited. Where a rule exists only by reference to SMPTE ST 336 or MISB ST 0107, it is NOT reconstructed from memory or from third-party sources: it is named as underivable and the park's closure stops there. Partial closure was a permitted outcome and partial closure is what happened - and 'partial' here means the tag half of the framing, not a fraction of a park.
framing_ruling_st_0601_14.how_the_verbatim_quotations_were_obtaine: Every quotation below was read positionally from the PDF's own text runs, line by line, and not from a reader-order dump. These PDFs store text with per-glyph kerning splits, so a naive extraction renders 'BER-OID' as 'BER - OID' and '16-Byte' as '16 - Byte'; the quotations here are the glyph runs joined in x-order within each line's own y, which reproduces the printed line exactly. The same method the tag table transcription used, and the reason it is stated again is that a quotation whose whitespace was repaired by judgement is a quotation with a judgement in it.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: The 16-byte Universal Label key of the UAS Datalink Local Set.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: SS 6.2, 'UAS Local Set Universal Label', PDF page 4. Restated by the deprecated ST 0601.8-19 block on PDF page 217.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: The UAS Local Set 16-Byte UL “Key” is registered in MISB ST 0807 [3] as: 06.0E.2B.34.02.0B.01.01.0E.01.03.01.01.00.00.00 (CRC 56773)
established_from_the_pinned_copy.second_statement_verbatim: ST 0601.8-18 (Deprecated) The UAS Datalink Local Set 16-byte Universal Key shall be 06 0E 2B 34 - 02 0B 01 01 - 0E 01 03 01 - 01 00 00 00 (CRC 56773)
established_from_the_pinned_copy.the_crc_is_carried_and_not_recomputed: The document prints a CRC beside every Universal Label it states and never states the polynomial. Recomputing one would need a rule from a registry this repository does not hold, and a check that invents its own algorithm checks the invention. So 56773 is recorded as the document's own value and is not verified.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: The packet is a Universal Label key, then the length of the value, then the value; the local set's items live inside the value.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: SS 6.3, 'UAS Datalink LS Packet Structure', PDF page 4, and Figure 1 on PDF page 5.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: Figure 1 illustrates the general structure of a UAS Datalink LS packet. A packet is a combination of a UL Key, the Length of the Value, and the Value. UAS Datalink LS items are encapsulated within the Value portion of the packet.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.figure_1_own_labels: UL Key (UAS Datalink LS) / 16 Bytes Identifier; Length of Value / BER Encoded; Value / UAS Datalink LS items / Variable Length; and beneath them 'BER-OID encoded Tag's', 'BER encoded Length's', 'Variable Length Data'. Read from the figure's own Form XObject text runs, which is why it can be quoted at all.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.what_it_does_not_give: The figure NAMES the length field as BER encoded and never says what BER encoding is. That is the whole of the residue below.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: Local Set tags are BER-OID encoded, one octet for 1 through 127 and two or more above 127.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: SS 7.1, 'UAS Datalink Local Set Items Summary', first bullet, PDF page 12.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: The “Tag” column is the KLV Local Set tag number for the item. The tag is an integer but encoded as a BER-OID value when used. Single-byte tags can represent tag numbers from 1 through 127. Tag numbers greater than 127 use two-bytes (or more).
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: klv_codec.decode_ber_oid and encode_ber_oid, over the established width range, exact inverses by exhaustion over 0..16383.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: The BER-OID bit pattern for a two-octet value: a leading continuation bit of 1 on the first octet and 0 on the second, seven payload bits each, fourteen bits of value.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: Figure 67, 'Status BER-OID bit pattern', PDF page 212, and the paragraph immediately beneath it.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.figure_67_own_labels: 'Status' / 'BER-OID' over two boxes labelled 'MSB Byte' and 'LSB Byte'; the MSB box carries a leading '1' and '(7 bits)', the LSB box a leading '0' and '(7 bits)'; the payload bits are numbered 6 5 4 3 2 1 0 under each. Read positionally from the figure's Form XObject.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: After decoding the Weapons Status BER-OID value, a 14-bit value remains.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.why_this_is_the_load_bearing_citation: SS 7.1 states WHERE the width changes and never says HOW a multi-octet BER-OID value is assembled. Figure 67 is the only place in the pinned copy that draws the continuation bit, and the '14-bit value' sentence is the only place that states the resulting capacity. Without them the two-octet form would have been inferred from examples rather than read, and klv_codec.BER_OID_MAX would have been a recollection.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: The tag encodings themselves, confirmed by worked example across the whole assigned space.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: The 'Example KLV Item (All Hex)' row of every item section in SS 8, PDF pages 31-217.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.what_was_measured: Every 'Tag Len Value' example row in the document was collected. The tag field takes exactly the values 01 through 7F for tags 1-127 and 8100 through 810D for tags 128-141 - 141 distinct encodings, no gap, no duplicate, and every one of them is what SS 7.1's boundary and Figure 67's bit pattern predict. 0x8100 is 128 and 0x810D is 141.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.why_it_is_evidence_and_not_the_rule: 141 examples cannot state a rule; they can only agree with one. They are recorded because they are the positive control on the reading above: a misunderstanding of the continuation bit would have disagreed with the document at 14 places.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: The packet checksum: a running 16-bit summation, its range, its algorithm, and what a receiver does when it fails.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: SS 6.6, 'Packet Checksum and Version Number', PDF pages 11-12; the algorithm again at SS 8.1.1.1 and a worked vector at SS 8.1.1.2, PDF page 31.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: To help prevent erroneous metadata from being presented with the Motion Imagery, a 16-bit checksum is included in every UAS Datalink LS packet as the last item. The checksum is a running 16-bit summation through the entire packet beginning with the 16-byte Local Set Key and ending with the length field of the checksum LS item (see Figure 7).
established_from_the_pinned_copy.algorithm_verbatim: unsigned short bcc_16 ( unsigned char * buff, //Pointer to the first byte in the 16-byte UAS Datalink LS key. unsigned short len ) //Length from 16-byte US key up to 1-byte checksum length. { unsigned short bcc = 0, i; // Initialize Checksum and counter variables. for ( i = 0 ; i < len; i++) bcc += buff[i] << (8 * ((i + 1) % 2)); return bcc; } // end of bcc_16 ()
established_from_the_pinned_copy.worked_vector_verbatim: 64 bits to checksum: 060E 2B34 0200 81BB / 060E + 2B34 = 3142 / + 0200 = 3342 / + 81BB = B4FD <-- Final Checksum
established_from_the_pinned_copy.requirements_verbatim: ST 0601.8-08 All instances of a UAS Datalink LS where the computed checksum is not identical to the included checksum shall be discarded. ST 0601.8-11 All instances of the UAS Datalink LS shall contain as the final item Tag 1, (Checksum).
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: klv_codec.bcc_16, transcribed loop for loop, masked to 16 bits because Python integers do not wrap where an unsigned short does. Checked against the document's own vector rather than against itself: the eight octets 060E2B34020081BB give 0xB4FD.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.the_half_that_is_still_blocked: SS 6.6 defines the checksum's RANGE in terms of 'the length field of the checksum LS item', so finding that end means walking the local set, which means the length grammar. bcc_16 therefore takes the range as an argument exactly as the standard's own C does, and this repository offers nothing that computes it. The algorithm is established; applying it to a real packet is not.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: A Zero-Length Item is a tag followed by a length of zero and no value, and it means the value is now unknown.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: SS 6.5, PDF page 10, and requirements ST 0601.14-32, -33 and -34.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: If a metadata producer needs to “shut-off” an item (i.e. make it immediately Unknown) the producer sends a Zero-Length Item (ZLI) which is a Local Set item with no value (i.e. tag followed by a length of zero, with no value).
established_from_the_pinned_copy.why_a_framing_fact_and_not_a_semantic_on: It is the one item shape where the VALUE is absent rather than opaque, so a walk that assumed every item has at least one value octet would desynchronise on it. Recorded here so that the walk, when it is written, is written knowing it. Not implementable now for the same reason nothing else is: a length of zero still has to be read as a length.

underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.rule: BER length encoding: the short form, the long form, and any constraint on which is permitted where.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.status: UNDERIVABLE FROM THE BYTES IN HAND. This is the residue, and it is the reason parks 4 and 8 do not close.

what_the_pinned_copy_does_say.names_the_two_forms_without_defining_eit: SS 6.3.2, PDF page 6, verbatim: 'A VLP is a group of items represented as length-value pairs with the item's tags suppressed. Lengths in BER short or long form precede each item's value as illustrated in Figure 2.' The same phrase recurs at SS 8.115, SS 8.122, SS 8.138 and SS 8.140, and not once is either form defined.
what_the_pinned_copy_does_say.figure_1_labels_the_field_and_stops: 'Length of Value / BER Encoded' and 'BER encoded Length's'.
what_the_pinned_copy_does_say.the_only_constraint_is_in_deprecated_tex: ST 0601.8-07 (Deprecated), Appendix A, PDF page 218, verbatim: 'All instances of item length fields within a UAS Datalink LS packet shall be BER Short form or BER Long form encoded using the fewest possible bytes in accordance with SMPTE ST 336 [2].' It is marked (Deprecated) in the document's own left column.
what_the_pinned_copy_does_say.the_live_route_is_a_second_delegation: ST 0601.8-03, SS 6.3.1, PDF page 5, verbatim: 'All UAS Datalink LS metadata shall be expressed in accordance with MISB ST 0107 [5].' So the rule was not deleted - it was moved out of ST 0601 and into ST 0107.3, which the revision history states in as many words: 'Deprecated Requirements ST 0601.8-02, -04, -05, -06, and -07 / ST 0107.3 includes these requirements as they apply to all MISB KLV based metadata (not just ST 0601)'.
what_the_pinned_copy_does_say.no_worked_example_reaches_long_form: Every 'Tag Len Value' example row in the document was collected and its length octet read. The distinct length octets are 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08, 09, 0B, 0E, 13, 14 and 24. THE LARGEST IS 0x24, which is 36. Not one example exercises long form, and not one even reaches the 127 a short form is usually said to stop at. So the examples are consistent with the familiar rule and cannot establish it: what they show is that a length in that set is written as a single octet equal to the length.

underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.why_the_examples_are_not_enough: A codec built from them would accept lengths 1-9, 11, 14, 19, 20 and 36 and have nothing to say about 10 or 200. That is a lookup table, not a grammar, and shipping it as a length codec would be the reconstruction this round was forbidden wearing an empirical costume.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.who_owns_it: PARK 8, SMPTE ST 336:2017, for the encoding; PARK 4, MISB ST 0107.3, for the formatting rule ST 0601 now routes through. Neither document is held.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.what_closes_it: Either document. Park 8 is a purchase decision and park 4 is a public download, so park 4 is the cheaper of the two and is the one a next round should take.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.implemented_as: klv_codec.decode_ber_length, encode_ber_length and walk_local_set all exist, are importable, and raise UnderivableFromPinnedCopy carrying this text. A reader who reaches for a length decoder gets the park number and the delegating sentence; a missing name would have given an AttributeError and an invitation to guess.

underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.rule: BER-OID encodings three octets wide and beyond.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.status: UNDERIVABLE. Bounded and small, and named rather than quietly extended.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.what_the_pinned_copy_does_say: SS 7.1: 'Tag numbers greater than 127 use two-bytes (or more).' SS 8.128's details, PDF page 193: 'Given a Wavelength Record FLP, the Wavelength ID in BER-OID format can be one or more bytes. The BER-OID format is self-describing providing the rules for obtaining the number of bytes for the value.' The document ASSERTS that the format is self-describing and never describes it beyond Figure 67's two octets.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.why_it_is_refused_rather_than_extended: Extending Figure 67's continuation pattern to a third octet is arithmetic anybody can do, which is exactly what makes it the tempting reconstruction. The pinned copy neither states the general rule nor works an example above two octets, and ST 0601's own tag space stops at 142 - so nothing in this standard would ever exercise it and nothing in this standard can settle it.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.what_it_costs_today: Nothing, for this local set: Table 1's highest tag is 141 and the two-octet form reaches 16383. It costs a future nested set whose own tags run higher, and it is recorded so that round knows the rule was never established rather than assuming it was implemented.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.implemented_as: klv_codec refuses a third continuation octet quoting the offset and naming parks 4 and 8. Fixture tag_third_continuation_octet records the refusal.

underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.rule: Whether a non-minimal BER-OID encoding must be REFUSED on parse.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.status: UNDERIVABLE AS A NORM, DECIDED AS AN IMPLEMENTATION, and the difference is stated rather than blurred.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.what_the_pinned_copy_does_say: ST 0601.8-06 (Deprecated), PDF page 218, verbatim: 'All instances of item Tags within a UAS Datalink LS packet shall be BER-OID encoded using the fewest possible bytes in accordance with SMPTE ST 336.' The requirement is real, it is in this document, and this document no longer asserts it on its own account - it moved to ST 0107.3 with the other four.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.the_decision: klv_codec.decode_ber_oid REFUSES the one non-minimal two-octet form, a leading 0x80. The reason is that accepting it would make two byte strings denote one tag, and a round trip over an ambiguous encoding is a statement about the codec rather than about the wire. It runs in the same direction as all 141 worked examples.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.what_is_not_claimed: That refusal is normatively required. The sentence requiring minimality is deprecated in this edition and its live successor is in a document this repository does not hold. If ST 0107.3 turns out to require acceptance, this is the decision that changes.

park_4.document: MISB ST 0107.3, KLV Metadata in Motion Imagery
park_4.what_this_round_established_about_it: That it is now the LIVE route rather than a parallel one. ST 0601.14 deprecated five of its own requirements into ST 0107.3 - ST 0601.8-02, -04, -05, -06 and -07 - and two of those five, -06 and -07, are precisely the tag-minimality and length-encoding rules this round went looking for. So park 4 is not merely 'formatting in motion imagery' as the delegation table has it: it now holds the framing constraints ST 0601 used to state itself.
park_4.why_it_does_not_close: Neither half of the shared exit condition is discharged. The document is not obtained, so it is not pinned, and no row set is written from it. Nothing about this round's reading of a DIFFERENT document changes that.
park_4.what_did_change_and_it_is_not_a_closure: Its pinned version is corroborated by a second document. ST 0601.14a's own reference [5] reads 'MISB ST 0107.3 KLV Metadata in Motion Imagery, Nov 2018', which is exactly what MISP-2019.1's Appendix B ref [14] pins. Two independent documents naming one revision is worth recording and is not worth a park state.

park_8.document: SMPTE ST 336:2017, Data Encoding Protocol Using Key-Length-Value
park_8.what_this_round_established_about_it: The precise size of what it owns, which was previously stated as 'key forms, the 16-byte Universal Label, the length forms' and is now narrower by two thirds. The 16-byte Universal Label of THIS local set is in ST 0601.14 SS 6.2 and needs no ST 336. The BER-OID tag form is in SS 7.1 and Figure 67 and needs no ST 336 for one and two octets. What is left to park 8 is the LENGTH grammar and the third BER-OID octet.
park_8.why_it_does_not_close: It is a purchase decision, the document is not held, and a narrower park is still an open park. Recording that a blocker shrank is not recording that it lifted.
park_8.what_did_change_and_it_is_not_a_closure: Its pinned version is corroborated the same way park 4's is: ST 0601.14a's own reference [2] reads 'SMPTE ST 336:2017 Data Encoding Protocol Using Key-Length-Value', matching MISP-2019.1's Appendix B ref [13] exactly. Worth noting because ST 0102.12's reference [3] pins ST 336:2007 instead - an older edition - which is a divergence between two delegated documents this repository holds, and is registered as KLV 11 below.

the_park_outcome.no_row_flipped: All 141 rows of tag_table_st_0601_14 remain 'not yet' and none of them was eligible to move: a framing rule says where an item begins and a row says what an item means. The round predicted no flips and there were none.
the_park_outcome.no_park_opened_and_none_renumbered: The roster is unchanged at twelve parks, one closed and eleven open, ten of the eleven public downloads and one a purchase. This round obtained no document and therefore had no occasion to change it.

what_was_implemented_and_what_deliberate.module: packages/cdm/synapse_cdm/adapters/klv_codec.py. A codec and NOT an adapter: no Adapter subclass, so no registry entry, no ordinal and no roster row. The framing layer cannot read a local set, and a module that registers as an adapter claims it can.
what_was_implemented_and_what_deliberate.the_injected_clock_seam: NAMED AND NOT BUILT, which is a deviation from the round's protocol and is recorded as one. In this package the clock is a parameter of Adapter.__init__ and codecs never take one - gmtif_codec and cat048_codec are the precedent. Creating an Adapter subclass to hold an unused seam would have claimed an ordinal and a roster row for something that cannot parse a length. The seam is built when there is an adapter to build it on.
what_was_implemented_and_what_deliberate.fixtures: fixtures/klv/framing/, thirteen fixtures and their twins, generated by fixtures/klv/spec/build_fixtures.py, which is the only thing that writes them. They are NOT adapter fixtures and the harness cannot replay one; they live in a subdirectory so that a harness run pointed at fixtures/klv still finds nothing and still fails, which is the state fixtures/klv/README.md describes.
what_was_implemented_and_what_deliberate.fixture_identities: UUID-v8 in the f1c7 namespace, identifying the FIXTURE and not anything in it, because a framing fixture's payload carries no identifiers at all.
what_was_implemented_and_what_deliberate.fixtures_omitted_and_why: Three classes, omitted rather than guessed, per the round's own rule that a fixture needing a rule this round could not establish is named in the residue: every length fixture including the truncated-length malformation; every key/length/value triple, which needs a length one rule up; and the 16383-to-16384 tag transition, which needs the third BER-OID octet. Writing any of them would have meant writing the rule first, from memory, and then testing this repository's memory against itself.
what_was_implemented_and_what_deliberate.bidirectionality: Claimed for what exists and checked by exhaustion rather than sampling: decode_ber_oid(encode_ber_oid(n)) == n for all 16384 values of the established range, and the key and checksum are equally exact. The whole range fits in a test, so there was no reason to sample it.
what_was_implemented_and_what_deliberate.no_tag_semantics_no_fusion_no_joins: Values are opaque octets throughout. Nothing in this module knows what tag 2 means, and nothing joins two items.

what_this_round_did_not_do: Did not obtain ST 0107.3 or SMPTE ST 336, and therefore closed no park.
Did not flip any of the 141 tag rows, none of which was eligible.
Did not open a park, renumber one, or change a reopen route.
Did not implement a length codec, a local-set walk, or any tag semantics.
Did not write a fixture whose octets needed a rule this round could not cite.
Did not create an Adapter subclass, and so did not claim an adapter ordinal.
framing_ruling_st_0601_14.SUPERSEDED_IN_PART_BY_THE_LENGTH_RULING: READ length_ruling_st_0107_3 BEFORE ACTING ON ANYTHING HERE. This node is the record of the framing round of 2026-08-26 and its statements were true of that round; three of them are no longer true of this repository. (1) Its park_4.state_after_this_round is OPEN, which was correct then - park 4 CLOSED later the same day. (2) Its underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand names three residues, and TWO are discharged: the BER length grammar and the third BER-OID octet are both stated by MISB ST 0107.3, now held. (3) Its third residue - whether a non-minimal BER-OID encoding must be refused - predicted 'If ST 0107.3 turns out to require acceptance, this is the decision that changes'; ST 0107.3 SS 6.3.1 forbids the octet by name, so the decision stands on live authority. THE NODE IS KEPT RATHER THAN REWRITTEN because it records what one document could establish alone, which is the finding that sent somebody to fetch the second one.

page_count_method.how: The page objects REACHABLE FROM THE CATALOG'S /Pages TREE, walked in /Kids order.
page_count_method.why_it_is_recorded: A page count is a pin value like any other, so the method that produced it has to be reproducible.
page_count_method.validated_before_it_was_trusted: Run against the seven documents whose page counts FORMAT_COVERAGE.md already records - eurocontrol-cat048-part4-edition-1-32.pdf 64, nato-aedp-4607-1-edition-a-v1.pdf 212, nato-aedp-4607-edition-a-v1.pdf 104, nato-stanag-4607-edition-4.pdf 6, nato-aedp-12-1-edition-a-v1.pdf 192, nato-aedp-12-edition-b-v2.pdf 150, nato-stanag-4676-edition-2.pdf 5 - and reproduced all seven exactly. The NATO documents keep their page objects inside compressed object streams and the EUROCONTROL one does not, so both paths are exercised by that check.
page_count_method.ruling: Ruled in FORMAT_COVERAGE.md, 'The page count, ruled from what a reader does with the number'. A page count is one term of a pin's identity row and its job is to let someone holding a copy check they hold the same document - which they do by opening it and seeing how many pages it has. So the count is the number of pages the document HAS, which is the page tree; a raw-object scan counts FILE OBJECTS, a different quantity that coincides only when a file has no orphaned page objects and no incremental update.
page_count_method.what_this_record_used_to_say_and_why_it_: It used to read: 'Counted from each PDF's own page tree - occurrences of /Type /Page across raw objects and across every inflated object stream.' That sentence names the PAGE TREE and then defines a RAW-OBJECT SCAN, which are two different methods; it was self-contradictory from the day it was written and nothing noticed, because the two agree on any file with no orphaned page objects and no incremental update. CAT034 Phase 1 found the first file where they disagree and recorded the divergence; the harmonisation round ruled for the page tree and rewrote this field. THE COUNTS IN THIS RECORD DID NOT MOVE - both methods give them - so this is a correction to the description of how they were obtained and not to the values.
page_count_method.recomputed_under_the_ruling: Every document in this repository with a recorded page count was recomputed under both methods: 11 pins, 3 CAT034 lineage editions, 22 CAT048 lineage editions. No pin moved. Three CAT048 LINEAGE entries moved - editions 1.28 and 1.29 from 58 to 56, edition 1.30 from 59 to 57 - and cat048_pin.json records each as a correction with the ruling cited.
page_count_method.how_this_rounds_two_counts_were_produced: SUPERSEDED BY THE FIELD BELOW and kept because the numbers it reports are still this record's. It read: run against the eight pins in this repository that are on disk and carry a recorded page count, the walker reproduced seven exactly - 31, 41, 64, 146, 5, 5 and 73 - and both new counts, ST 0601.19 at 226 and ST 0102.12 at 18, are additionally method-independent.
page_count_method.a_disagreement_found_outside_this_row_se: WITHDRAWN on 2026-08-26, and recomputed_under_the_ruling stands unqualified. This field used to open 'AND THE FIELD BELOW IS FALSE, at one document' and report that fixtures/cat062/spec/eurocontrol-asterix-cat062-p9-appendix-a-ed13.pdf is recorded as 25 pages while the ruled method gives 23, with objects 1760 and 1782 as orphans whose reachable /Parent does not list them and with the file's own top /Pages node stating /Count 23. THE 23 HAS A NAME: it is a SUPERSEDED GENERATION of the page tree, read as if it were current. The file is linearized and then INCREMENTALLY UPDATED once - three %%EOF markers, the original body ending at the 247816 bytes the linearization dictionary declares as /L - and that update redefines exactly three objects, all of them page-tree nodes, inside object stream 1805 at offset 1078590. The superseded generation, in object stream 80 at offset 246459 in the pre-update body, is 1723 /Count 23, 1724 /Count 5 /Kids [1731 1 7 9 12] and 1727 /Count 8 /Kids [43 45 47 49 51 53 55 57]. The generation the xref chain actually names is 1723 /Count 25, 1724 /Count 6 /Kids [1760 1731 1 7 9 12] and 1727 /Count 9 /Kids [43 45 47 49 51 53 55 57 1782]. A walk that takes an object's FIRST definition in file order rather than the one the xref chain resolves to reads the superseded tree, counts 23 leaves, and reports the two pages the update ADDED as orphans - which is the reading that was recorded here. Both added pages are real pages: A4 /MediaBox 595.32 x 841.92, with 11 355 and 805 bytes of decoded content stream. The linearization dictionary's own /N 23 is the pre-update page count and is preserved because an incremental update does not rewrite linearization parameters, so it corroborates the sequence rather than the count. not_committed.the_streams_are_not_in_git_either_and_th: ADDED 2026-08-26 BY THE WALK ROUND. fixtures/klv/streams/ holds a real MPEG-2 transport stream (102 004 664 bytes) and the 977-octet KLV extraction taken from it, and NEITHER IS TRACKED. The exclusion is a DIRECTORY rule - `fixtures/klv/streams/` in .gitignore - and not an extension rule, which is the opposite of the choice made for the PDFs above, so the difference is worth stating rather than leaving to inference. An extension rule works for the PDFs because every file in a spec/ directory is one of three known extensions and a new document is the ordinary case. A stream has no such extension discipline: the transport container arrived as .mpg, the extraction is .klv, and a future round could hold .ts or .mpeg or a raw PID dump - so an extension rule would be a list somebody has to remember to extend, and the failure mode of forgetting is that a hundred-megabyte binary enters the index. The directory rule cannot fail that way. BOTH FILES ARE PINNED BY SHA-256 in walk_ruling_real_stream_2026_08_26.the_two_pins, and the extraction's command is recorded there and was RE-RUN rather than recalled, so a reader who obtains the transport stream can reproduce the 977 octets exactly and check both hashes. AMENDED 2026-08-26 BY THE PROVENANCE ROUND: this is NO LONGER THE ONLY DIRECTORY RULE. fixtures/klv/provenance/ joins it on the same pattern and for a stronger version of the same reason - see the_fetched_provenance_evidence_is_not_in_git_either_and_it_is_a_THIRD_RULE. The sentence above about the PDFs' extension rule still holds and the streams rule did not move; what changed is that 'a DIRECTORY rule' now describes two rules rather than one, and a reader who met this field alone would have inferred otherwise. ALSO AMENDED: the sentence 'a reader who obtains the transport stream can reproduce the 977 octets' had no way of saying WHERE to obtain it, because this pin carried no origin. It does now - see walk_ruling_real_stream_2026_08_26.the_two_pins.transport_stream.origin_url.
not_committed.the_fetched_provenance_evidence_is_not_i: ADDED 2026-08-26 BY THE DAY FLIGHT PROVENANCE ROUND. fixtures/klv/provenance/ holds NINETEEN fetched files - Wayback CDX index dumps, archived pages of the MISB's own website, that site's machine-readable publication catalogues, and the sample collection's directory listings, root README and index - and NONE IS TRACKED. The exclusion is a DIRECTORY rule, 'fixtures/klv/provenance/' at .gitignore:121, which is the choice made for the streams and the OPPOSITE of the choice made for the PDFs, and the reason is the streams' reason and more so: fetched evidence has no extension discipline at all. This round alone landed .txt CDX dumps, .html archived pages, .xml site catalogues and one extensionless 00-README, and the next round could hold .json or a bare header dump. An extension rule would be a list somebody has to remember to extend, and the failure mode of forgetting is that somebody else's website enters the index. WHY THE FILES ARE HELD RATHER THAN READ AND DISCARDED: the standing rule is that every asserted fact comes from bytes held and pinned, and a quotation from a page that was read and thrown away is a recollection. Each is pinned by SHA-256, byte count and origin URL at day_flight_provenance_2026_08_26.the_held_evidence_nineteen_files_each_pinned.files. git check-ignore -v was run on every one and each reports '.gitignore:121:fixtures/klv/provenance/'.
