ambiguity_register.KLV 1: The promulgation lag. The wrapper's cover, Letter of Promulgation and reference are all dated 30 July 2020; the profile it promulgates carries November 2018 on its title page and in the footer of all 73 pages. Twenty months, unexplained in either document. Sharpened by the profile's own FORWARD versioning rule, which makes the '2019' in MISP-2019.1 an identifier rather than a date - so citing this content by year is ambiguous between 2018 printed, 2019 in the identifier and 2020 promulgated. Consequence adopted: every citation names the document by identifier and hash, never by date.
ambiguity_register.KLV 2: Every requirement ID inside MISP-2019.1 names an earlier profile version. TWO COUNTS, EACH STATED UNDER ITS OWN BASIS, re-derived from the pinned copy at writing time. DISTINCT IDENTIFIERS: 120 occur and NONE is MISP-2019.1-nn - MISP-2015.1 84, MISP-2018.1 17, MISP-2016.1 8, MISP-2018.3 4, MISP-2018.2 3, MISP-2017.1 3, MISP-2015.3 1, summing to the 120. OCCURRENCES: 129 in total - MISP-2015.1 93, with the other six families identical to their distinct figures because MISP-2015.1 is the ONLY family whose identifiers repeat, nine repeats across its 84. The prefix records the profile version that INTRODUCED the requirement, not the document carrying it, so MISP-2015.1-07 is a live requirement of MISP-2019.1. Consequence adopted: requirements are cited by their own ID with the pinned document named beside them, because an ID alone reads to a NATO reader as a citation of MISP-2015.1 - which STANAG 4609 Edition 4 promulgated and Edition 5 superseded. || THE ARITHMETIC WAS REPAIRED 2026-08-28 AND THE CONCLUSION WAS NEVER IN DOUBT. This entry read '120 distinct requirement IDs occur' and then gave a distribution - MISP-2015.1 93, MISP-2018.1 17, MISP-2016.1 8, MISP-2018.3 4, MISP-2018.2 3, MISP-2017.1 3, MISP-2015.3 1 - THAT SUMS TO 129. The headline was the DISTINCT count and the distribution was the OCCURRENCE count, spliced into one sentence. BOTH FIGURES WERE CORRECT UNDER THEIR OWN BASIS and neither was stated with it, and the splice was invisible for six of the seven families because only MISP-2015.1 repeats - so the one bucket that could reveal it was the only one that did. THE DEFECT WAS ARITHMETIC FRAMING AND NOT THE CONCLUSION: 120 distinct, none MISP-2019.1-nn, and the consequence above stands exactly as adopted. STABLE UNDER NORMALIZED COUNTING, checked rather than assumed: no requirement ID wraps a line in the pinned copy, so raw and whitespace-normalized text yield 129 and 120 alike and the whitespace defect did not produce these figures.
ambiguity_register.KLV 3: The profile's reference to the STANAG is one edition behind and its Appendix C is one edition ahead. Appendix B ref [1] is 'NATO STANAG 4609: NATO Digital Motion Imagery Standard, Edition 4, 19 Dec 2016' and SS 1.1 sends the reader to [1] for NATO-specific requirements; Appendix C.1.2 discusses 'STANAG 4609 Edition 5 as represented in MISP-2019.1'. So within one document the STANAG is both Edition 4 and Edition 5, and the wrapper actually holding this profile is Edition 5, which supersedes Edition 4. A reader following SS 1.1's pointer lands on the superseded edition.
ambiguity_register.KLV 4: External context, and explicitly not an error: the NISP is a year behind the chain. NISP Volume 1, ADatP-34(L) / Version 12, 19 Jul 2019, 182 pages, lists NATO STANAG 4609 as 'Ed 4' against 'Standard - MISP-2015.1'. That NISP version predates STANAG 4609 Edition 5 by a year, so it is stale by chronology rather than by mistake - which means a programme taking the NISP as its authority would implement MISP-2015.1 and be conformant to a superseded STANAG. The copy read hashes to 12a3b2ab7075390b9edd53fb50538f5a7098c0d8f0a9a69c8af894acb40e1bac, 1440024 bytes, and is NOT in fixtures/klv/spec/ - so that hash stands on the reading that recorded it and is the one value here a later re-verification cannot check. Same treatment AEDP-12 Edition A (2014) gets in the NITS pin: history, never a basis.
ambiguity_register.KLV 5: The reference list versions most of its MISB documents and six not at all. A revision suffix is given for every document this row set relies on (0601.14, 0102.12, 0603.5, 0107.3, 0903.4, 0806.4, 1402.2, 1201.3, 1303.1, 1204.1, 0902.8) and none for ref [74] 'MISB ST 1607 Constructs to Amend/Segment KLV Metadata, 2016', ref [89] 'MISB ST 1101', ref [84] 'MISB RP 1302' or the three TRMs at refs [98], [99], [100]. ST 1607 is the one that bites: MISP-2017.1-95 is a 'shall' whose target names no revision.
ambiguity_register.KLV 6: Nothing in the profile requires a standalone metadata stream to carry an absolute time. The unconditional mandate MISP-2018.3-116 attaches to a Motion Imagery FRAME; the metadata mandate MISP-2018.1-97 is conditional on a timestamp being present; the prose in SS 2.1.5 introducing both is circular - 'it is also mandatory for Metadata packets which include a Metadata item for a timestamp based on Absolute Time'. The two unequivocal predecessors MISP-2015.1-03 and MISP-2015.1-04 are in Appendix A.2 as DEPRECATED. SS 5.5 then contemplates the case that falls through: 'There are situations where Metadata needs to be transmitted separately from the Motion Imagery.' Consequence: Event.observed_at for this format is not merely blocked on park 3, it may be absent from the source - which is gap 23.
ambiguity_register.KLV 7: The security mandate's paragraph and its requirement do not use the same term, and Appendix E defines both. SS 4.4.2.9 says 'It is mandatory that Motion Imagery Data be marked correctly and consistently with security classification' and 'The approved practices in this standard are mandatory for all Motion Imagery Data'; the requirement it introduces, MISP-2015.1-73, says 'Motion Imagery shall include Security Metadata'. Appendix E defines 'Motion Imagery Data' as 'Three components: Motion Imagery (see definition below), Metadata and/or Audio' and 'Motion Imagery' as a sequence of pictures. So the paragraph's scope includes a metadata stream and the requirement's scope is the imagery, which decides whether this adapter's input must be labelled at all.
ambiguity_register.KLV 8: The document classified as 'related' is the one that 'defines the required data items'. STANAG 4609 Ed 5 puts the Motion Imagery Handbook under OTHER RELATED DOCUMENTS while its AGREEMENT clause names only MISP-2019.1, and MISP SS 1.3 calls the Handbook a companion 'providing definitions of terms used with more background and technical detail'. But SS 3.6.7 says of the same document that it 'defines the Structure of the Common Metadata System (CMS), describes how to organize the sensor/platform data into a hierarchy of KLV Packs and Local Sets that reduces the bandwidth needed to transmit the data, and defines the required data items'. A document that defines required data items is normative in fact. Park 10 records that whoever obtains it answers this first.
ambiguity_register.KLV 9: A pinned copy whose cover does not describe its contents, and the first ambiguity in this record found by a check nobody asked for. ST 0601.19's cover reads 'MISB ST 0601.19' and '02 March 2023'; its revision history table carries two rows dated AFTER that cover date - 05/10/2024, changing Figure 17's corner 4 tag values, and 06/11/2025, resolving 'item 42 ambiguity (i.e., MSL or HAE)' - and the file's /CreationDate is 2 July 2025. The document's own section 2 states the convention it is not following: a corrected document 'will have a single letter Minor Version appended to the Major Version number', as ST 0001.2 becomes ST 0001.2a, and the MISB 'will not update the referring document with the Minor Version number change'. So there exist at least three distinct documents all correctly cited as 'ST 0601.19', a citation by edition number cannot distinguish them, and the same section warns that 'when acquiring any MISB reference listed below from an NGA repository the latest version may be either a Major or Minor Version'. WHAT IT BOUNDS: it does not affect this round's ruling, which stops on .14-versus-.19 and would stop identically whichever .19 copy were held. What it bounds is the claim a pin makes - which is why this record's SHA-256 is the identity of a COPY and not of an edition, and this is the first document in this repository where those two come apart. ST 0102.12 was checked the same way and does not have the problem: one revision-history row, and it is the cover date.
ambiguity_register.KLV 10: THE SAME COMING-APART AS KLV 9, MET AT FETCH TIME INSTEAD OF BEING DISCOVERED LATER, and one turn worse in each of two ways. MISP-2019.1 cites 'MISB ST 0601.14'; the NSG Registry serves that edition as ST0601.14a.pdf; the file's cover reads 'MISB ST 0601.14a' and '1 May 2020' while the edition the citation names is dated 1 November 2018 by the document's own revision history. WORSE THE FIRST WAY: the copy carries a THIRD revision-history row, dated 08/19/2021, whose Revision cell is EMPTY - checked from the page's drawn column geometry, not from a text dump - and the file's /CreationDate is 17 December 2021. ST 0601.19's two undeclared amendments at least sat under a stable edition number that a citation could name; this one has no string at all, so there is no citation any document could make that would distinguish it. WORSE THE SECOND WAY: this local set carries its own version number on the wire. Item 65, UAS Datalink LS Version Number, is MANDATORY in every packet and states the revision of ST 0601 the producer encoded against - and it is a uint8, one value per MAJOR revision, so it cannot express a Minor Version letter either. The format's own answer to 'which edition made this?' has exactly the same blind spot as the citation. WHAT IT BOUNDS: nothing in the row set, and that is checkable rather than hopeful - the 'a' changed one thing, 'Corrected table headers in Item 47 - Generic Flags', and the 08/19/2021 row changed four things all described as editorial, none of which touches a tag, a length or a format. What it bounds is what a pin can CLAIM, which is why the SHA-256 is the identity of a copy and the filename keeps the letter the registry served. See KLV 9, which is the same hazard in the document this one supersedes-by-five.
ambiguity_register.KLV 11: THREE DELEGATED DOCUMENTS THIS REPOSITORY HOLDS PIN ST 336:2017 AND ONE PINS ST 336:2007, and it was found by reading reference lists this round had no other reason to read. MISP-2019.1's Appendix B ref [13] reads 'SMPTE ST 336:2017 Data Encoding Protocol Using Key-Length-Value' and ST 0601.14a's own reference [2] reads the same string - so the profile and the field dictionary agree. ST 0102.12's reference [3] reads 'SMPTE ST 336:2007 Data Encoding Protocol Using Key-Length-Value', a DIFFERENT EDITION, and it is not decorative there: ST 0102.12-65 says 'The Security Metadata Universal Set shall conform to SMPTE ST 336 KLV encoding rules' and ST 0102.12-66 says the same of the Local Set. WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS REGISTERED RATHER THAN RESOLVED: park 8 is a single row naming a single edition, and these are two. A round that buys ST 336:2017 will hold the grammar ST 0601's items are framed under and will NOT hold the one ST 0102's security items are required to conform to, and this record cannot say whether the two editions differ in any way that reaches a length octet - because neither is held. NOT A CONTRADICTION IN EITHER DOCUMENT: each is internally consistent and each pins what was current when it was written, ST 0102.12 in June 2017 and ST 0601.14 in November 2018. It is a divergence between two delegations of one profile, which is a fact about the profile's reference set rather than about either standard. WHAT IT BOUNDS: park 8's exit condition, which now has a question in it that the parks table's 'obtain the EXACT version the delegation table pins' does not answer, since the delegation table pins one edition and two of the held documents pin two. Recorded, not acted on: changing a park's exit condition on the strength of a reference list read in passing is the roster change smuggled into a reading that the park 1 round refused to make. UPDATED 2026-08-26 BY THE LENGTH ROUND, AND THE COUNT MOVED FROM TWO-AGAINST-ONE TO THREE-AGAINST-ONE: MISB ST 0107.3's reference [1] reads 'SMPTE ST 336:2017 Data Encoding Protocol Using Key-Length-Value', agreeing with ST 0601.14a's ref [2] and MISP-2019.1's Appendix B ref [13]. ST 0102.12's ref [3] STOOD ALONE at :2007 OVER THE SET HELD ON 2026-08-26, which is the scope that sentence was true under and is now stated rather than implied - see the 2026-08-28 amendment below, which is where it stopped being true. THE STRENGTHENED MAJORITY DOES NOT RESOLVE IT and the reason is worth stating: ST 0102.12 is the document whose security items are REQUIRED to conform to its edition (ST 0102.12-65 and -66), so a majority of other documents naming a different edition does not relieve a reader of ST 0102's requirement. What did change is that the edition park 8 should buy is now named by three of the four held documents rather than two, which makes the purchase decision easier and the ST 0102 question no easier. || AMENDED 2026-08-28 BY THE REPAIR ROUND, AND THE ORIGINAL STANDS AS A DATED CLAIM. The sentence above was TRUE WHEN WRITTEN and is false today, and what falsified it is this repository's own later acquisition rather than any error in the reading. ST 1204.1 and ST 1301.2 were pinned on 2026-08-27, and both name the older edition: ST 1204.1's reference [10] reads 'SMPTE ST 336:2007 Data Encoding Protocol Using Key-Length-Value' and ST 1301.2's informative reference [2] reads 'SMPTE ST 336-2007 Data Encoding Protocol Using Key-Length-Value'. THE TALLY OVER THE PROFILE'S PINNED DELEGATION SET IS NOW FOUR-AGAINST-THREE, re-derived from held bytes at writing time: :2017 at MISP-2019.1 ref [13], ST 0601.14a ref [2], ST 0107.3 ref [1] and ST 1303.1 ref [1]; :2007 at ST 0102.12 ref [3], ST 1204.1 ref [10] and ST 1301.2 ref [2]. ST 0601.19's ref [1] also reads :2017 and is EXCLUDED from the tally, because this record holds it as CONTEXT ONLY under reconciliation_ruling.ruling_st_0601 and never as a delegation the profile pins - counting it would make the reading five-against-three and would be counting a document the row set is forbidden to read semantics from. THE ENTRY'S REASONING SURVIVES ITS OWN SENTENCE, and that is why this is decay rather than error: this entry already explains the divergence as 'each pins what was current when it was written', and the two new witnesses CORROBORATE that explanation while refuting the count - ST 1204.1's cover is 24 October 2013 and ST 1301.2's is 27 February 2014, so both predate SMPTE ST 336:2017 outright and could not have named it. WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE UNQUALIFIED is the closing clause about the purchase decision: the edition park 8 should buy is named by FOUR of the seven held documents that date this reference rather than by three of four, and a bare majority is a weaker argument for the purchase than a three-to-one one. THE ST 0102 QUESTION IS UNCHANGED AND UNCHANGEABLE BY COUNTING, for the reason the 2026-08-26 amendment already gives: ST 0102.12-65 and -66 require ITS OWN items to conform to the edition IT names, and no majority elsewhere relieves a reader of that. A DERIVATION NOTE THAT IS PART OF THE FINDING: ST 1301.2 writes 'ST 336-2007' with a HYPHEN where every other held document writes a colon, so the first sweep for this - keyed on 'ST 336:' - missed it and found only ST 1204.1. The tally above was re-derived with a form-tolerant pattern over whitespace-normalized text, and both readings agree.
ambiguity_register.KLV 12: A HELD DOCUMENT'S REQUIREMENT IDENTIFIERS DO NOT ALL CARRY ITS OWN EDITION NUMBER, and citing them as though they did would cite strings the document does not contain. MISB ST 0107.3 states thirteen requirements. Eleven are prefixed ST 0107.3 (-03 through -13) and TWO are prefixed ST 0107.2: 'ST 0107.2-01 Bit order shall be big-endian or msb' and 'ST 0107.2-02 Byte order shall be big-endian or MSB', both in section 6.1. NOT AN ERROR IN THE DOCUMENT: MISB stamps a requirement with the edition that introduced it, and this edition's own revision history says it 'Added requirements -03 through -13', which confirms -01 and -02 came from ST 0107.2 - registry document 4149, which 0107.3 supersedes. So the numbering runs continuously across editions and the prefix is provenance rather than a typo. WHY IT IS REGISTERED RATHER THAN NOTED IN PASSING: klv_codec.decode_ber_length reads its long-form payload big-endian on ST 0107.2-02's authority, and it is the ONLY octet-order requirement in the whole delegation chain - ST 0601.14a never states one. A citation this load-bearing that is easy to normalise to 'ST 0107.3-02' is exactly the miscitation that gets made once and then propagates to five sites. HOW TO CHECK IT: the two requirement blocks sit under section 6.1 on PDF page 2 and print the 0107.2 prefix in the document's own left column.
ambiguity_register.KLV 13: A HELD DOCUMENT NAMES ASN.1 AS THE SOURCE OF THE BER RULES AND PINS THE PART OF ASN.1 THAT DOES NOT CONTAIN THEM. MISB ST 0107.3 SS 6.3.3.1 says, verbatim: 'Items using "ber" types in the MISB standards use the ASN.1 [4] Basic Encoding Rules for Lengths rules.' And SS 6.3.1 says of tags: 'The Basic Encoding Rules (BER) for an Object Identifier (BER-OID) as defined in ASN.1 [4] is the method selected for encoding a Local Set tag', and later 'ASN.1 forbids the use of 0x80 in the first byte of a BER-OID value'. Its reference [4] reads 'ITU Rec X.680 (08/15) Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1): Specification of basic notation'. X.680 SPECIFIES NOTATION; the Basic Encoding Rules are X.690. So the document attributes an encoding rule to the ASN.1 recommendation that defines syntax rather than encoding. WHY IT IS REGISTERED AND NOT RESOLVED: neither X.680 nor X.690 is held, so this repository cannot say whether X.680 (08/15) contains anything that bears on BER lengths, nor whether the citation is a slip or a convention of the series. IT IS NOT A CONTRADICTION IN ST 0107.3 - the document is internally consistent and says the same thing in both places. WHAT IT BOUNDS, AND THIS IS WHY IT MATTERS: park 8's reopen condition reads 'A PURCHASE DECISION, NOT A DOWNLOAD' because SMPTE paywalls ST 336. ITU recommendations are free. If the BER rules the two remaining residues need - the meaning of a zero length-of-length, and any ceiling on length octets - are in X.690 rather than in ST 336, then part of the one park that costs money is a free download. NOT ACTED ON: the reference needs adjudicating first, and changing a park's reopen route on a reference list read in passing is the roster change the park 1 round refused to make. A round that wants park 8 cheaper starts here.
ambiguity_register.KLV 14: THE FORMAT CARRIES A MANDATORY EDITION STAMP ON THE WIRE AND NO HELD EDITION SAYS WHICH ITEMS EACH EDITION ADMITS. MISB ST 0601 requires item 65 in every packet (ST 0601.8-12) and SS 8.65 defines its value as the document's own major revision, '1..255 corresponds to document revisions MISB ST 0601.1 thru MISB ST 0601.255'. So every conforming packet declares the edition it was written against, and a reader that wanted to honour that declaration would need to know WHICH ITEMS THAT EDITION DEFINES. NEITHER HELD COPY PROVIDES IT, IN EITHER DIRECTION. ST 0601.14a's revision history begins at edition 14 and ST 0601.19's at edition 19; no item section in either carries an introduction annotation; Table 1's own column list - Tag, Name, Units, Format, Len, SDCC, MUL, Description - has no edition column; and the one dating device the series does carry, the requirement-identifier prefix, is stamped only from edition 8 onward, so ST 0601.14a's 33 distinct identifiers span editions 8, 9, 10, 13 and 14 and NONE reaches editions 1 through 7. WHAT IT BOUNDS: reconciliation_ruling had already recorded, looking FORWARD from .14, that the requirement delta to .19 is enumerable from the stamps but 'does not bound the ITEM delta, and the item delta is the one a tag table would need'. The walk round looked BACKWARD from .14 to .1 and met the same wall from the other side. So the item delta is not enumerable in EITHER direction from anything held, and the stamp a conforming emitter is REQUIRED to send cannot be acted on by a reader holding these documents. NOT A CONTRADICTION - no held sentence disagrees with another - and NOT RESOLVABLE HERE: it is resolved by holding the editions themselves, which for edition 1 is PARK 13. It is the reason that park exists and the reason the walk round ended in a park rather than a ruling. || AMENDED 2026-08-27 BY THE PARKS ROUND, AND THE AMENDMENT ABOVE IS PARTLY REFUTED. The park-13 closure concluded that 'the wall is made of unobtained documents rather than of undocumented history - the editions state their own deltas perfectly well'. The second half is false, and the documents that refute it were on disk when it was written: they landed in spec/history/ at 20:42 on 2026-08-26 and the amendment was written the same day. THE CHECK, which needs no changelog at all: an edition's item SET is readable from its own SS 7 / SS 8 subsection headers, and six editions are held. Enumerated, contiguous, no gaps in any of them - EG0601 initial release 1..39 (39); EG 0601.1 1..72 (72); STD 0601.4 1..80 (80); MISB ST 0601.8 1..95 (95); ST 0601.14a 1..141 (141); ST 0601.19 1..143 (143). EDITION 1'S CHANGELOG BALANCES EXACTLY: 'Added metadata items 40 through 72', and 39 + 33 = 72, confirmed at both endpoints - which is what park 13's closure leaned on and it holds. EDITIONS 2 THROUGH 4 DO NOT. Eight items separate edition 1 from edition 4 (73-80) and ST 0601.4's SS 3 accounts for FOUR: the RVT nesting tag at .2 (73), and at .3 the VMTI nesting tag (74) plus the 'Reference Ellipsoid Height versions of Sensor and Alternate Platform heights' (75, 76). Items 77 Operational Mode, 78 Frame Center Height Above Ellipsoid, 79 Sensor North Velocity and 80 Sensor East Velocity are named in NO SS 3 row - the words 'operational' and 'velocity' occur nowhere in that section - and .4's own row adds no item. So the surviving changelog is INCOMPLETE WHERE IT EXISTS, not merely absent where it does not. WHAT IT BUYS: the item set is known exactly at six editions rather than two, editions 2 and 3 are bounded between 72 and 80 with four of eight additions attributed, and the wall is now editions 5, 6, 7 and 9 through 13 and 15 through 18 - fourteen, none held. The pricing changes with it: obtaining an edition buys its TABLE, because a table always states itself; it does not reliably buy its DELTA. A reader honouring a stamp of 0x0B still has nothing to consult, which is this entry's point and is untouched. || CORRECTED FURTHER 2026-08-27 BY THE BUMP-GATE ROUND, and the correction is to the refutation rather than to the amendment. The refuting block above was headed THAT LAST CLAUSE and then quoted the MIDDLE one. The amendment's conclusion ends in three clauses: (a) the wall is made of unobtained documents rather than of undocumented history; (b) the editions state their own deltas perfectly well; (c) which makes this entry a park list rather than a defect in the standard. (a) was corrected, (b) was the clause quoted and refuted, and (c) - the conclusion the amendment was FOR - was never adjudicated. RULED HERE, from held bytes: (c) IS FALSE IN THE EXCLUSIVE FORM IT STATES. ST 0601.4's SS 3 exists to log revisions, its own first bullet being 'Added section 3 for modifications and changes' inherited verbatim from edition 1, and four of the eight item additions between editions 1 and 4 appear in no row of it. A revision log that omits half the additions it was created to record is a defect in the document, first-hand, in a document this repository holds. THE CORRECTED FORM: this entry is BOTH a park list - fourteen editions unheld, and their tables are what a reader honouring a stamp needs - AND a record of a drafting defect, because the one surviving changelog that reaches back to the initial release does not account for what it logs. The words that fail are 'rather than': the two are not alternatives, and the amendment's case rested on their being alternatives. WHAT IS UNCHANGED: the park is still worth its price and for the same reason, because an edition's item SET is readable from its own subsection headers whether or not its SS 3 is complete. What changes is only what this entry is a record OF.
ambiguity_register.KLV 15: THE DOCUMENT THE STANDARD TELLS A READER TO CONSULT FOR EDITION 1 DOES NOT EXIST UNDER THAT NAME. ST 0601.14a SS 8.65 defines item 65's value as '1..255 corresponds to document revisions MISB ST 0601.1 thru MISB ST 0601.255', so a reader honouring an on-the-wire stamp of 0x01 is sent to 'MISB ST 0601.1'. NO SUCH DOCUMENT WAS EVER PUBLISHED: edition 1 of the series is MISB EG 0601.1, an ENGINEERING GUIDELINE dated 15 May 2008 on its cover, and the series became a Standard at 0601.2 - ST 0601.4 SS 3 states the conversion outright ('Change the status from Engineering Guideline to Standard in order to enforce requirements upon developers implementing this document'). The standard has renamed its own history, and SS 8.65's range projects the ST name back across twelve editions that did not carry it. EDITION 1 SAYS SO ITSELF, from the other side: its own SS 7.65 states the identical range as 'EG0601.1 thru EG0601.255'. WHAT IT COST: park 13 was opened, described, guarded by a test and cited from three files under the name 'MISB ST 0601.1', and the name was wrong in every one of them - which is not a drafting slip in this repository but SS 8.65's own naming, adopted without checking that the document existed. IT ALSO NEARLY COST THE FETCH: the Wayback CDX index holds no ST0601.1.pdf at gwg.nga.mil because that filename never existed, and the document was found at /misb/docs/eg/EG0601.1.pdf only after the search was widened past the name the park gave it. NOT A CONTRADICTION between held sentences - SS 8.65 and SS 7.65 describe the same range and the series really did change status - and RESOLVED for this repository's purposes: park 13 is closed on EG 0601.1, which is the document SS 8.65's '0601.1' denotes, and the closure says so in as many words rather than quietly correcting the name.
ambiguity_register.KLV 16: EDITION 1 DISAGREES WITH ITSELF ABOUT ITS OWN DATE, AND ST 0601.4 DISAGREES WITH IT AGAIN. EG 0601.1's cover prints '15 May 2008' and no page header or footer in its 98 pages carries a date, so the cover is its sole statement and under provenance_ruling.what_the_edition_date_field_means it governs the pin's edition_date field. Its own SS 3, however, carries TWO rows for EG0601.1 - '13 December 2007' and '15 May 2007' - which puts the row described as 'Editorial changes only' seven months BEFORE the substantive one, and puts it a year before the cover. ST 0601.4's SS 3 restates the same first row as '13 December 2006', which makes the sequence coherent (13 Dec 2006, then 15 May 2007) and disagrees with edition 1's own text by a year. So of the three readings available, the two that are internally coherent are the ones edition 1 does NOT state. NOT RESOLVED AND DELIBERATELY SO: nothing held decides which year is the typo, the pin records the cover date because the ruling says the document's own cover governs, and NO RULING IN THIS REPOSITORY RESTS ON THE DATE - park 13 turned on a Len column, not on a calendar. Recorded because the pin states one date and the document contains three, and a reader checking the pin against the PDF will meet the other two. || THE COVER DATE IS CORROBORATED FROM INSIDE THE DOCUMENT ON 2026-08-27, by a route nobody had tried: edition 1's own reference list. EG 0601.1's SS 2.3 cites 'MISB RP 0102.5, Security Metadata Universal and Local Sets for Digital motion Imagery, 15 May 2008'. WHAT THAT PROVES, EXACTLY: a document cannot cite a reference published a year after itself, so the held bytes CANNOT be the 15 May 2007 issue - the copy pinned here is the 15 May 2008 one, and any reading in which this PDF is the 2007 issue is dead. The edition_date field does not move; what moves is its standing, from a value ELECTED by provenance_ruling to a value CORROBORATED at a second site inside the same 98 pages. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, and this entry declines to round up: WHY SS 3 reads 2007. Two readings survive and the bytes do not separate them - (a) SS 3's year is a one-digit typo and the row is the cover's own issue, or (b) there was a real 15 May 2007 editorial issue and the document was re-issued on 15 May 2008 without SS 3 gaining a row for it. (a) IS THE BETTER READING AND IS NOT A PROOF: two issues falling on the same day and month a year apart is a coincidence where a single mistyped digit is the commonest defect in this register, and SS 3 exists to log revisions - its own first row is 'Added section 3 for modifications and changes' - so a re-issue it does not log is a defect of the same size as the typo it would replace. UNDER EITHER READING ST 0601.4's SS 3 DOES NOT REPAIR THAT ROW: it restates 2007. So this entry's own sentence that .4's restatement 'makes the sequence coherent' is true of ONE of the two rows, and that is this round's correction to it. TWO FURTHER ANCHORS, both first-hand: the initial release is 12 January 2006 at two independent sites (EG 0601's cover and ST 0601.4's SS 3), and ST 0601.4's SS 3 dates STD 0601.2 to October 29, 2008. STILL UNDECIDED: both SS 3 rows, for different reasons - the '15 May' row is narrowed to two readings, and the '13 December' row is UNTOUCHED, 13 December 2007 by edition 1's SS 3 against 13 December 2006 by ST 0601.4's, with nothing held separating them at all. NO RULING IN THIS REPOSITORY RESTS ON THE DATE and that has not changed. || EXTENDED FROM HELD BYTES 2026-08-27 BY THE BUMP-GATE ROUND, AND THE '13 DECEMBER' ROW IS NO LONGER UNTOUCHED. This entry's 'nothing held separating them at all' is now false, and what separates them is SS 3's own ROW ORDER. The list runs, in both held copies and in the same order: EG0601 initial release 12 January 2006; EG0601.1 13 December 2007 (ST 0601.4 restates 13 December 2006); EG0601.1 15 May 2007. The first row fixes the list as chronological, oldest first. Under ST 0601.4's 2006 the three rows are in order; under edition 1's own 2007 they are NOT, because 13 December 2007 would follow 15 May 2007 and the list would run backwards across its last two rows. So one reading makes the section internally consistent and the other makes it wrong twice, in the same sentence and in its position on the page. EVIDENCE AND NOT PROOF, on this register's standing discipline: a list can be misordered and nothing held says this one is not. What it is no longer is undecided-on-nothing, and the row order points the same way ST 0601.4 does. A THIRD CORROBORATION OF THE COVER DATE, from the file rather than the page: EG 0601.1's PDF document-information dictionary reads /CreationDate D:20080515125829 with /ModDate IDENTICAL to it, so the file was produced once on 15 May 2008 at 12:58:29 and never re-saved, and its /Title carries the source filename EG0601.1_UAS_Local_Data_Set_20080515.doc, a second date stamp in the same field. THE FIELD WAS CALIBRATED AGAINST THE LINEAGE RATHER THAN ASSUMED: across the four held 0601 documents /CreationDate equals the cover date exactly for EG 0601.1, ST 0601.4 and ST 0601.8 and post-dates it by four days for the initial release, whose cover reads 12 January 2006 against D:20060116085414 in the file. So in this series the field tracks the cover with one known lag of four days, which is what makes the agreement a corroboration rather than a coincidence of two unrelated numbers. WHAT THE TWO READINGS NOW COST: reading (a), that SS 3's '15 May 2007' is a one-digit typo for the cover's own issue, needs ONE mistyped digit copied forward into ST 0601.4's SS 3 along with the rest of the row, whose bullets .4 reproduces verbatim. Reading (b), a real 15 May 2007 editorial issue re-issued 15 May 2008 without SS 3 gaining a row, now needs TWO documents to fail to log the same re-issue - edition 1's own SS 3, and ST 0601.4's SS 3 four editions later, which carries exactly the same two EG0601.1 rows and no third while having taken the trouble to correct the 13 December year. A round that read only edition 1 could not see that second cost. (a) REMAINS THE BETTER READING AND REMAINS UNPROVEN, and this entry's refusal to elect it stands. STILL UNDECIDED AFTER THIS ROUND: the '15 May' row between (a) and (b) with (a) preferred on a wider margin, and the '13 December' row NARROWED AND NOT CLOSED - the row order and ST 0601.4 both say 2006, edition 1 says 2007, and no held document states which was typed wrongly. NO ACQUISITION WAS ATTEMPTED FOR THIS ENTRY and none was needed: all of it is read out of two PDFs already pinned and held. Note the designation in the citation: RP 0102.5, not ST 0102.5. The 0102 series converted Recommended Practice to Standard exactly as the 0601 series converted Engineering Guideline to Standard, so this is KLV 15's phenomenon one series over - and it is what made the delegation-table gate refuse the edit until the revision was declared.
ambiguity_register.KLV 17: TWO EDITIONS FILL THE FORMAT COLUMN OF ITEMS 11 AND 12 DIFFERENTLY, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS A CHARACTER ENCODING. ST 0601.14a SS 8.11 and SS 8.12 both state a KLV Format of 'utf8' with a Max Length of 127. MISB EG 0601.1 SS 7.11 and SS 7.12 both state 'ISO7' with a stated range of '1..127', and edition 1's Table 1 writes the same two items as 'String ISO7'. THIS IS THE ONLY COLUMN THAT MOVED. The witnessed-set round of 2026-08-26 read all 26 witnessed items at both ends of a twelve-year span - edition 1 (15 May 2008) and .14a (1 May 2020) - and every other Units, Range and Format cell agrees. WHAT IT COSTS: nothing on any octet either edition admits, because ISO 646 is a strict subset of UTF-8 by construction, so klv_uas_codec decodes both as UTF-8 - the PINNED edition's statement, which reconciliation_ruling requires. WHAT IT WOULD COST IF IGNORED: an emitter written against edition 1 sending a high-bit octet meant as an 8-bit code page produces a value that is not valid UTF-8, and decode_value refuses it naming this entry. The pinned stream says nothing either way - its own items 11 and 12 are pure ASCII ('EON', 'IR', 'Geodetic WGS84'). NOT A CONTRADICTION BETWEEN HELD SENTENCES: the series changed its own encoding somewhere in the twelve revisions between the two, and which revision is a question no held changelog answers - the .5, .6, .7 and .9-through-.13 gap the park 13 adjudication round already named. || NARROWED FROM TWELVE REVISIONS TO FIVE ON 2026-08-27, and the intermediate step turns out not to be an encoding change at all. This entry was written from the two ENDPOINTS of the span; the lineage holds two documents INSIDE it. Items 11 and 12, Format column, verbatim, at all six held editions: EG0601 initial release 'String ISO7' (and 'String 1..127 ISO7' in the item blocks); EG 0601.1 'String 1..127 ISO7'; STD 0601.4 'String 1..127 ISO7' - UNCHANGED AT EDITION 4; MISB ST 0601.8 'String 1..127 ISO 646' - A THIRD SPELLING; ST 0601.14a 'utf8'; ST 0601.19 'utf8'. EDITION 8'S 'ISO 646' IS A RENAMING AND NOT A CHANGE, and edition 8 is the document that proves it: its reference [16] is 'ISO/IEC 646:1991, Information Technology - ISO 7-bit coded Character Set for Information Interchange' - the standard 'ISO7' had denoted for eight editions without ever citing it. So the column moved TWICE and only the second move is an encoding change: ISO7 -> ISO 646 between editions 4 and 8, naming the same character set, and ISO 646 -> utf8 between editions 8 and 14. The gap shrinks from .2-through-.13 to .9-through-.13, five revisions, none held. AND THE REFERENCE WENT WITH THE COLUMN: ST 0601.14a's reference list contains no ISO 646 entry at all - '646' occurs twice in its 218 pages and neither occurrence is a reference - so the edition that adopted utf8 dropped the normative reference for the encoding it replaced rather than superseding it in place. ONE RESIDUE, inside a single edition rather than between two: ST 0601.8 states the Format as 'ISO 646' in the item blocks and still carries the note '- ISO7 character set.' at three sites in the same document. Both spellings denote reference [16], so it is a drafting residue and not a contradiction - and it is the evidence that edition 8 is the RENAMING edition, because it is the one edition where the old spelling and the new one appear together. COSTS NOTHING on any octet any of the six editions admits, for the reason above; klv_uas_codec is unchanged.
ambiguity_register.KLV 18: A HELD DOCUMENT'S REQUIREMENT IDENTIFIERS DO NOT SAY WHICH EDITION STATES THEM, AND ONE OF THE 26 SAYS IT WRONG. MISB ST 1402.2 states 26 requirements. TWENTY-FIVE are prefixed with the bare series number - they read 'ST 1402-NN', with no revision suffix at all - so a requirement's own identifier does not say which edition of ST 1402 states it. Re-derived from the pinned bytes at writing time rather than copied from the closing round's report: the 26 distinct identifiers extracted from delegated_specifications_held.st_1402_2's copy run -01 through -26 contiguously, 25 unsuffixed and one not. THE TWENTY-SIXTH READS 'ST 1402.1-26' - suffixed, and suffixed with the PREVIOUS edition, inside the edition-2 document that carries it. WHY THIS IS ITS OWN ENTRY AND NOT AN AMENDMENT TO KLV 12. KLV 12 records the converse shape in ST 0107.3: eleven requirements carry their own edition's number and two carry the preceding edition's, which that entry rules is PROVENANCE rather than error, because MISB stamps a requirement with the edition that introduced it and ST 0107.3's own revision history confirms it from the other side. HERE THE MAJORITY IS THE UNSUFFIXED FORM, so the same explanation cannot be reached: if the suffix were provenance then 25 of 26 requirements would be claiming no provenance at all. DELIBERATELY NOT ADJUDICATED. Whether 'ST 1402.1-26' marks the edition that introduced requirement 26 - the KLV 12 reading - or is a drafting slip is not decidable from this document alone, and NO OTHER EDITION OF ST 1402 IS HELD. A precedent exists that would decide it the KLV 12 way, and one precedent is not a reading. WHAT IT COSTS, WHICH IS WHY IT IS REGISTERED RATHER THAN NOTED IN PASSING: this is the SAME defect one layer in. This record already logs that MISP-2019.1 cites 'MISB ST 1402 [48]' with no revision suffix at SS 3.6.9.1 and SS 5.3.1, which is why the delegation table has to cite Appendix B to get the version. A reader who follows the profile's unsuffixed citation into the document finds the document's own requirements unsuffixed too, so at no point in the chain does an identifier carry its edition - and the pin's SHA-256 is the only thing in this repository that says which text a 'ST 1402-05' quoted here came from.
ambiguity_register.KLV 19: FOUR REQUIREMENTS ARE WITHDRAWN AS RE-SPECIFICATIONS AND NOT AS FACTS, AND THE FOUR VALUES THEY CARRY ARE THE ONES THAT LOCATE A KLV STREAM. MISB ST 1402.2 deprecates four of its 26 requirements - ST 1402-05, -06, -19 and -23 - leaving 22 live. Re-derived from the pinned bytes at writing time. Verbatim, with the '(Deprecated)' marker as the document prints it: 'ST 1402-05 (Deprecated) For the Synchronous Metadata Multiplex Method, the stream_id shall be 0xFC, indicating “metadata stream.”'; 'ST 1402-06 (Deprecated) For the Synchronous Metadata Multiplex Method, the stream_type shall be 0x15, indicating “Metadata carried in PES packets”.'; 'ST 1402-19 (Deprecated) For the Asynchronous Metadata Multiplex Method, the stream_id shall be 0xBD, indicating “private_stream_1.”'; 'ST 1402-23 (Deprecated) For the Asynchronous Metadata Multiplex Method, the stream_type shall be 0x06, indicating “PES packets containing private data.”'. THE DISTINCTION IS THE ENTRY, AND THE DOCUMENT STATES IT ITSELF. Section 3's revision history gives the reason in its own words: 'Deprecated REQ’s -05, -6, -19, -23; these are required by ISO/IEC 13818-1 and should not be re-specified here.' So what was withdrawn is MISB's ACT OF REQUIRING these values, on the ground that ISO/IEC 13818-1 already requires them. THE VALUES THEMSELVES ARE UNCHANGED AND STILL APPLY - they are simply somebody else's to state. WHY IT IS REGISTERED. A reader who reads 'deprecated' as 'no longer applicable' - the ordinary reading, and the one a reader in a hurry takes - would discard the stream_type and stream_id for BOTH multiplex methods, which is precisely and exactly the ability to FIND the KLV elementary stream inside an MPEG-2 transport stream. That ability is what park 9 existed to buy. So the entry records that the deprecation is a change of WHO STATES A FACT and not a change of the fact, because the two readings differ by the whole value of the document. NOTE the identifier defect running through the quotations: all four are of the unsuffixed form KLV 18 registers, and the document's own revision history writes the second of them as '-6' where the requirement itself prints '-06'. AND A SECOND INSTANCE OF THE SAME MOVE IS NOW HELD: ST 1303.1, pinned 2026-08-27, deprecates a requirement of its own 'as it is a definition' and renames its Appendix A to 'Deprecated Requirements'. Recorded as an observation inside this entry rather than as a reading - two documents in one delegation chain using deprecation for something other than obsolescence is a pattern worth watching and is not yet a rule about the series.

parks.how_many: Thirteen parks over fifteen documents, and FOUR are CLOSED - park 1, park 4, park 13 and park 9. Nine remain open, eight of them public downloads and one a purchase. PARK 9 CLOSED 2026-08-27 BY THE OFF-PEAK ROUND, and it is the first park in this table closed by an acquisition that earlier rounds attempted and could not make: three attempts met HTTP 429 and the fourth, asked at a different hour, met HTTP 200. PARK 13 CLOSED 2026-08-26 BY THE ADJUDICATION ROUND, on the same day it was opened by the walk round, and it is the only park in this table that opened and closed inside one day. It is also the only one a STREAM asked for rather than a document: it was a superseded revision of a document this repository already holds at a later edition, which under this repository's own rule - a later revision is a different document - makes it a fifteenth document and not a re-read of the third. THE FIFTEENTH DOCUMENT TURNED OUT NOT TO BE NAMED WHAT THIS TABLE CALLED IT: there is no MISB ST 0601.1, edition 1 is MISB EG 0601.1, and the park closed on that document - see ambiguity_register KLV 15 and park_13_ruling_2026_08_26. THE DELEGATION COUNT DOES NOT MOVE AND IS NOT THE SAME COUNT: the profile delegates to FOURTEEN documents, park 13's document is not one of them, and a park's document and a profile's delegation are different things. THE NUMBERING DOES NOT MOVE: the parks are cited by number from the row sets, from the fixture plan and from the register, so a closed park keeps its number and its row and says it is closed, and a new park extends the numbering rather than filling a gap. Renumbering to close a gap would silently re-point every citation, which is a larger lie than a table with three closed rows in it.
parks.honest_strength: Of the nine that remain open, eight are public downloads and one is not. That is materially weaker than the two blockers this repository already carries - GMTIF's Annex L, which reads '(TO BE PROVIDED)' in the promulgated text, and the NITS XSD, which the Custodian re-issues on its own revision axis and distributes through national representatives. It is closer to CAT048's Reserved Expansion Field: obtainable, and simply not obtained. PARKS 1, 4 AND 13 ARE THE PROOF OF THAT CLAIM RATHER THAN EXCEPTIONS TO IT - the largest park in the table, the cheapest, and the narrowest were all closed by one person with a browser, which is what 'obtainable, and simply not obtained' predicts. Park 4 is the sharpest of the three proofs: it was SIX PAGES, it had been sitting behind a free download since November 2018, and it held the rule that stopped this repository reading a KLV stream at all. PARK 13 IS THE SECOND-SHARPEST AND IT SHARPENS A DIFFERENT EDGE: its document was not behind a free download at all - both official routes refuse an automated GET - and it was obtained anyway, from a mirror of the publisher's own host, which says that 'obtainable' can survive the publisher's front door being shut and that the honest cost of that is a provenance caveat rather than a stop. See delegated_specifications_held.eg_0601_1.source_is_a_MIRROR_and_not_the_registry. PARK 9 IS THE FOURTH PROOF OF THE SAME CLAIM AND THE SHARPEST: it was not closed by finding a new route or a new document, but by asking the SAME route for the SAME document at a different hour. 'Obtainable, and simply not obtained' turned out to include 'obtainable, and asked at the wrong time of day' - which is the cheapest failure mode in this table and the one least visible to a round that records a refusal faithfully.
parks.shared_reopen_route: The profile's FORWARD prints it: 'References developed by the MISB are available under MISB Public Web Site: http://www.gwg.nga.mil/misb or NSG Registry Web Site: https://nsgreg.nga.mil/misb.jsp'. No NSO gate, no national representative, no account.
parks.shared_exit_condition: For parks 2, 3, 5-7 and 9-12: obtain the EXACT version the delegation table pins (not 'the current one' - the profile pins a revision and a later revision is a different document); pin it in fixtures/klv/spec/ by SHA-256, byte count and page count with its title-page identity read; then write the row set that document supports. HOW THE SECOND HALF READS FOR A DOCUMENT WITH NO ROWS: park 4 closed on a standard that defines no tag table, and 'the row set that document supports' was read as 'the artefact this document makes writable' - a codec, for a framing standard. See length_ruling_st_0107_3.the_park_outcome.park_4.why_the_second_half_was_not_waived_and_how_it_was_read.

the_one_that_is_not_a_download.reopen_condition: A PURCHASE DECISION, NOT A DOWNLOAD. SMPTE is a commercial standards body and ST 336 sits behind a paywall, which the profile concedes in its own register: 'Commercial references cited in this document are available from industry organizations.' The other nine open parks need somebody to spend an afternoon; this one needs somebody to spend money, and a table reporting both as 'obtain the document' would hide the only entry that has to go to a person with a budget. LAST CHECKED 2026-09-03, AND THE CHECK REFUTED THIS FIELD - see the_premise_was_refuted_2026_09_03, which is adjacent deliberately, because a withdrawal a sweep does not land on is a withdrawal nobody reads.

the_premise_was_refuted_2026_09_03.WHAT_WAS_FOUND: SMPTE'S OWN DOCUMENT LIBRARY SERVES ST 336 FREELY, AND THIS PARK'S NAME FOR ITSELF IS NO LONGER TRUE. At 2026-09-03T10:34:27Z pub.smpte.org/doc/st336/ answered HTTP 200 with a version listing naming two publications, 2017-07-21 and 2007-08-22 - which are the two editions this record's own KLV 11 entry sets against each other. At 10:35:03Z the 2017 artefact route, pub.smpte.org/doc/st336/20170721-pub/st336-20170721-pub.zip, answered HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/zip and Content-Length 419570, from SMPTE's own host behind CloudFront, with no sign-in, no membership check and no purchase step anywhere on the route.
the_premise_was_refuted_2026_09_03.WHAT_IS_REFUTED_AND_WHAT_IS_NOT: REFUTED: the treatment claim that this park is 'a purchase decision, not a download', that it is 'the one park in this table that is not a download', and that it 'needs somebody to spend money' where the others need an afternoon. NOT REFUTED: the profile's own FORWARD sentence about commercial references, which this row QUOTES - it is a quotation of what the profile says and stays true as one. The defect is this repository's INFERENCE from that quotation, carried for as long as nobody asked the publisher's own host. A concession in a 2019 document about commercial availability is evidence about 2019 and was read as a standing fact about a paywall.
the_premise_was_refuted_2026_09_03.HOW_IT_WAS_FOUND_AND_THE_ROUTE_MATTERS: BY DATING AN UNDATED FIELD, ON RULE 12'S FIRST SWEEP. The reopen condition stated a cost in the present tense with no instant behind it, so it was one of the sweep's findings; re-reading it meant asking the route, and asking the route refuted it. THE PARKS GATE HAD ALREADY MARKED THIS ROW AS ITS OWN BLIND SPOT: gates/parks_table.py's blocker_existence() reports NOT DERIVABLE for this row because the document is not a MISB four-digit series, and prints it as the surface its exit code does not cover. So the gate named the row a human had to read, and the human read it and found it wrong - which is the split working rather than failing.
the_premise_was_refuted_2026_09_03.AND_THE_RECORD_POINTED_THE_NEXT_ROUND_AT: This row ends 'A round that wants this park cheaper starts at KLV 13' - the ITU substitution, on the reasoning that BER is ASN.1 and ITU recommendations are free. That pointer is now superseded and is NOT deleted: KLV 13's reasoning was sound and its conclusion was too weak, because the cheap route was never a substitute document at all. It was the publisher. A summary cell that redirects the next sweep is the disease README rule 10 names, and this is an instance of it that was CORRECT when written and pointed somewhere worse than the truth.
the_premise_was_refuted_2026_09_03.NOTHING_WAS_ACQUIRED_AND_THIS_IS_STOPPED: The artefact route was asked with HEAD and nothing else - zero body bytes were transferred, no zip was fetched, no document was pinned, and this park is still OPEN. Acquisition is not a round's own call here, which is the discipline the STANAG 4586 edition ruling was reached under: the fork is put up and somebody rules on it. THE FORK: pin ST 336:2017 from SMPTE's own library and close park 8, or leave it parked. The second question rides on the first and is why the ruling is worth having rather than obvious - KLV 11 sets ST 0102.12's reference to ST 336:2007 against three documents pinning 2017, and BOTH editions are on that listing, so a round that acquires can settle KLV 11 in the same act or can acquire 2017 alone and leave it open.
the_premise_was_refuted_2026_09_03.WHAT_THIS_DOES_NOT_TOUCH: No tag row moves. Park 8's two residual absences - 0x80 as a first length octet, and any ceiling on the count of length octets - are still absences in ST 0107.3 and neither is reachable from a conforming stream, so the length codec's completeness argument is unchanged in every term. What changed is the PRICE of answering them, not the answer.

the_one_that_is_not_a_download.what_the_length_round_learned_about_this: IT SHRANK AGAIN AND IT DID NOT MOVE. MISB ST 0107.3 - a free six-page download - states the length grammar and the BER-OID chain rule, so what park 8 still owns is two ABSENCES in ST 0107.3 rather than a grammar: 0x80 as a first length octet, and any ceiling on the count of length octets. Neither is reachable from a conforming stream. AND THE COST MAY NOT BE WHAT THIS FIELD SAYS: ST 0107.3 SS 6.3.3.1 sources the BER length rules to ASN.1 [4], an ITU recommendation, and ITU recommendations are free. That is registered as KLV 13 and NOT acted on here, because its reference [4] is X.680 - notation - where BER is X.690, so the citation needs adjudicating before this field is rewritten.

length_ruling_st_0107_3.what_this_is: THE LENGTH RULING, 2026-08-26, and the round that discharged the residue the framing ruling named. The framing round asked ST 0601.14a for three framing rules, got two, and recorded the third as UNDERIVABLE with the sentence that delegated it. This round followed that sentence. ST 0601.8-03 - 'All UAS Datalink LS metadata shall be expressed in accordance with MISB ST 0107 [5]' - points at MISB ST 0107.3, six pages, and that document states the length grammar on its own account. PARK 4 IS CLOSED. Park 8 stays OPEN and is narrower again.
length_ruling_st_0107_3.the_document_rule_this_round_worked_unde: Unchanged from the framing round, and it had to be, because the trap inverted. The framing round's hazard was somebody supplying the familiar BER length rule from memory. This round's hazard is that ST 0107.3's rule IS the familiar rule - so a codec written from memory would have passed every test. What separates the two is that every clause below is derived from octets the document prints, and the derivation is written out example by example so a reader can check it against six pages rather than take it. Had ST 0107.3 said something else, the same method would have produced something else.
length_ruling_st_0107_3.the_question_this_round_was_SENT_to_answ: Park 4's half of the length residue, in four parts: the short-form/long-form rule, the long-form length-of-length octet, any stated ceiling on length octets, and any constraint on which form an encoder may emit. The fourth was the one that decided park 4, because 'free choice' and 'minimal encoding required' produce different codecs and the framing round could not tell which ST 0107.3 required.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: The short form: for lengths below 128, one octet, and the octet IS the length.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: For example, encoding the length of two (2), a value less than 128, with long form uses two bytes (0x8102) instead of the short form one-byte (0x02) length.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.how_it_is_derived: The document prints 0x02 as the short form of 2 and names 'values less than 128' as the range for which long form is the wasteful choice. So 0..127 is one octet with no flag bit to strip.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: The long form: the first octet's low seven bits are the COUNT of following octets, and those octets are the length big-endian.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: SS 6.3.2, PDF page 4, for the form; ST 0107.2-01 and ST 0107.2-02 in SS 6.1, PDF page 2, for the octet order.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: BER is an efficient encoding of a length; however, by either using the long form for values less than 128, or by prepending a long form value with zero-byte values, BER becomes less efficient. For example, encoding the length of two (2), a value less than 128, with long form uses two bytes (0x8102) instead of the short form one-byte (0x02) length. Another example is encoding the value 128 with padded zeros (0x8300 0080) instead of the optimized value with two bytes (0x8180).
established_from_the_pinned_copy.how_it_is_derived: THE DERIVATION WRITTEN OUT, because this is the clause a recollection would have supplied. The passage prints four encodings of two lengths: 0x02 -> 2 short form; 0x81 0x02 -> 2 long form with ONE following octet; 0x81 0x80 -> 128 long form with ONE following octet; 0x83 0x00 0x00 0x80 -> 128 long form with THREE following octets. 0x81 introduces one and 0x83 introduces three, so the low seven bits of the first octet are a count. The document also states how it COUNTS: it calls 0x8180 'two bytes' and 0x8102 'two bytes', so the introducer is included in the total. The following octets are big-endian by ST 0107.2-02, 'Byte order shall be big-endian or MSB'. Two data points plus an octet-order requirement fix the shape uniquely, and nothing is imported from outside the document.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.second_statement_verbatim: ST 0107.3-05 All instances of item Length fields within a MISB defined KLV Universal or Local Set shall be BER Short form or BER Long form encoded using the fewest possible bytes.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: klv_codec.decode_ber_length and encode_ber_length. Fixtures length_long_form_lowest (8180, the document's own), length_long_form_two_octets and length_non_minimal_padded_zeros (83000080, the document's own).

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: Minimal encoding is REQUIRED. An encoder does NOT choose freely between the forms.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: ST 0107.3-05, SS 6.3.2, PDF page 4. LIVE text, not deprecated.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: All instances of item Length fields within a MISB defined KLV Universal or Local Set shall be BER Short form or BER Long form encoded using the fewest possible bytes.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.this_is_the_answer_to_park_4s_question: YES to minimality, NO to free choice. And it is the same sentence ST 0601.14a carries as ST 0601.8-07 with two edits: the onward delegation 'in accordance with SMPTE ST 336 [2]' is REMOVED, and the scope widens from 'a UAS Datalink LS packet' to 'a MISB defined KLV Universal or Local Set'. ST 0601.14a's revision history said the content moved here 'as they apply to all MISB KLV based metadata (not just ST 0601)'; this is the content, and it arrived without the delegation. So the constraint is ST 0107.3's own and does not route onward to park 8.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.what_it_makes_possible: A TOTAL encoder with no form selector. For every length there is exactly one conforming encoding, so encode_ber_length takes the length and nothing else - the ruling is enforced by the signature rather than by a check. test_the_length_codec_is_total_because_st_0107_3_05_leaves_no_choice_of_form asserts the parameter list.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: klv_codec.decode_ber_length refuses both non-minimal forms as KLVFramingError; encode_ber_length cannot express either.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: The two non-minimal forms, named and refused: long form for a value below 128, and leading zero octets.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: by either using the long form for values less than 128, or by prepending a long form value with zero-byte values, BER becomes less efficient
established_from_the_pinned_copy.why_exactly_two_and_not_a_general_policy: Because the document names exactly two and works an example against each. A codec refusing 'non-minimal encodings' in general would be enforcing a rule nobody wrote; a codec refusing these two is enforcing SS 6.3.2's sentence. They happen to be exhaustive over the long form - a long-form encoding is minimal iff its value is at least 128 and its leading octet is non-zero - and that they coincide is worth stating rather than relying on.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: Two KLVFramingError branches, each quoting the document's own example against the octets in hand. Fixtures length_non_minimal_long_form (8102) and length_non_minimal_padded_zeros (83000080).

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: A zero length is legal, and the Value is then absent rather than empty.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: The Length defines the number of bytes used by the Value. Lengths are usually positive numbers; however, a zero length is possible in unique cases. Values are the binary representation describing a specific item. In the case of a zero Length, the Value is not a part of the item (see MISB ST 0601 [3]).
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: encode_ber_length(0) is 0x00 and walk_local_set advances past such an item without consuming a value octet. Fixtures length_short_form_zero and item_zero_length.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: The BER-OID chain rule for ANY width, which is the '(or more)' ST 0601.14a SS 7.1 named and never defined.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: BER-OID tags are one or more bytes linked together in chain fashion. In BER-OID a zero in the Most Significant Bit (msb) position terminates the tag's chain. For example, when the msb is set to zero in the first byte, this forms a one-byte tag number ranging from 0x00 to 0x7F. When the msb of the first byte is set to one, the second successive byte becomes part of the BER-OID chain. In continued fashion, if the second byte's msb is set to one, the next byte becomes part of the chain. This pattern continues until the msb of a final byte in the chain is zero. Together the seven Least Signification Bits (lsb) of each byte in the chain form the tag number.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.second_statement_verbatim: Using BER-OID for the tags in all MISB local sets enables efficient tag encoding and unlimited future growth.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.this_was_a_residue_of_the_framing_round_: The framing round recorded 'BER-OID encodings three octets wide and beyond' as UNDERIVABLE and refused a third continuation octet, on the ground that extending Figure 67's pattern was 'arithmetic anybody can do, which is exactly what makes it the tempting reconstruction'. SS 6.3.1 states the general rule, so the extension is now a transcription. decode_ber_oid follows the chain and encode_ber_oid emits any non-negative integer.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.what_this_cost_in_the_codec: BER_OID_MAX_OCTETS is DELETED - a cap beside a codec that no longer honours it is a constant nothing reads. BER_OID_MAX is KEPT at 16383 and re-documented as a waypoint rather than a limit: it is what the delegating document could prove alone, and the exhaustive round-trip test still runs over it because the range fits in a test.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: klv_codec.decode_ber_oid and encode_ber_oid. Fixture tag_three_octet_lowest (818000 -> 16384) REPLACES the refusal fixture tag_third_continuation_octet (818100).

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: Non-minimal BER-OID tags are forbidden, on LIVE authority.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: To prevent BER-OID from including leading zeros, ASN.1 forbids the use of 0x80 in the first byte of a BER-OID value.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.this_is_a_PROMOTION_and_not_a_behaviour_: decode_ber_oid already refused a leading 0x80. The framing round recorded that refusal as 'UNDERIVABLE AS A NORM, DECIDED AS AN IMPLEMENTATION' because the only sentence requiring tag minimality in ST 0601.14a was ST 0601.8-06, marked (Deprecated), and it wrote: 'If ST 0107.3 turns out to require acceptance, this is the decision that changes.' IT DID NOT. ST 0107.3 forbids the octet by name, so the refusal is now transcribed rather than decided. The behaviour is identical and the provenance is not, and the caveat is recorded as discharged rather than deleted.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.one_honest_wrinkle: SS 6.3.1 attributes the prohibition to ASN.1 rather than asserting it as a numbered ST 0107.3 requirement - 'ASN.1 forbids'. So it is live prose in a held document reporting a rule from a document this repository does not hold. That is materially stronger than a deprecated requirement and materially weaker than a 'shall', and it is recorded at that strength rather than rounded up. Registered as KLV 13, which also notes that the reference it points at is X.680.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: klv_codec.decode_ber_oid's leading-0x80 refusal, whose message now quotes SS 6.3.1 and names ST 0601.8-06 as the deprecated predecessor. Fixture tag_non_minimal_two_octets.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: Bit and byte order are big-endian, KLV-wide and retroactively.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: SS 6.1, 'Bit and Byte Order', PDF page 2. NOTE THE PREFIX: these two requirements are numbered ST 0107.2, not ST 0107.3.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: ST 0107.2-01 Bit order shall be big-endian or msb. / ST 0107.2-02 Byte order shall be big-endian or MSB.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.why_the_prefix_is_0107_2: MISB stamps a requirement with the edition that introduced it, and this edition's revision history says it 'Added requirements -03 through -13'. So -01 and -02 came from ST 0107.2 - registry document 4149, which 0107.3 supersedes - and keep their prefix. Citing them as ST 0107.3-01/-02 would cite strings this document does not contain.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.what_it_bears_on: decode_ber_length reads a long-form payload big-endian on ST 0107.2-02's authority, and it is the only octet-order rule in the chain: ST 0601.14a never states one. So the length codec's endianness is cited to a requirement whose number is not this edition's, which is exactly the sort of thing that gets miscited once and then propagates.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: int.from_bytes(payload, 'big') in klv_codec.decode_ber_length, with the requirement quoted at the line.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: A decoder must skip items it does not recognise, using the Length to find the next one.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: Applications which decode MISB KLV Local Sets shall skip unknown Local Set values so as to not impact the decoding of known Local Set items within the same Local Set instance.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.supporting_prose_verbatim: One advantage of KLV is the ability to skip or ignore items which may not be known by a consumer of the data. For example, suppose a new version of a Local Set introduces new tags which an existing decoder does not understand. Instead of crashing, the decoder simply ignores any item it does not understand - this makes a decoder 'future-proof'. In such cases, the Length specified by the Tag is used to skip the correct number of bytes to the next item.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: walk_local_set satisfies it STRUCTURALLY rather than with a skip list: it knows no tags at all, so every item is equally unknown to it and the caller decides what it recognises. The 141-row tag table is in this file and nothing in klv_codec consults it.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: ST 0107.3 is a RESTRICTING profile of SMPTE ST 336, not a deferral to it.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: SS 6.2, 'SMPTE KLV', PDF page 2, and ST 0107.3-03.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: The MISB standards define requirements which incur limits on the full SMPTE 336, making the MISB standards a profile of the SMPTE standards.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.second_statement_verbatim: ST 0107.3-03 All Local Set KLV metadata shall be formatted in compliance with SMPTE ST 336 [1].
established_from_the_pinned_copy.why_this_matters_to_park_8: It is the answer to the round's question 'does 0107.3 add any constraint of its own on top of the delegation'. YES, and ST 0107.3-05's minimality is that constraint. Which is why the length codec is COMPLETE AND TOTAL with park 8 still open: the delegation widens what ST 336 would allow and ST 0107.3 narrows it, and the narrowed grammar is fully stated here.

underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.rule: 0x80 as a FIRST LENGTH OCTET - a long form declaring zero following octets.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.status: UNDERIVABLE FROM THE BYTES IN HAND. PARK 8. The one residue in the length grammar and the reason park 8 is not closed by this round.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.what_the_pinned_copy_does_say: NOTHING, and the silence is the finding. SS 6.3.2 defines the short form and the long form and never mentions a count of zero. In BER this is the INDEFINITE-LENGTH form, whose meaning is SMPTE ST 336's - and naming it as such is already at the edge of what this repository may assert, which is why the codec refuses rather than describing.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.the_delegating_sentence_verbatim: ST 0107.3-03 All Local Set KLV metadata shall be formatted in compliance with SMPTE ST 336 [1].
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.does_0107_3_add_a_constraint_on_top_of_t: NO, not for this octet. It adds ST 0107.3-05's minimality, which bears on every OTHER long form and cannot reach this one: 0x80 encodes no length at all, so 'fewest possible bytes' has nothing to compare. This is the one place in the grammar where the profile's restriction does not cover the delegation's surface.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.why_it_costs_nothing_today: A conforming encoder never emits it - ST 0107.3-05 makes every length's encoding unique and none of them is 0x80 - so the octet is unreachable from any stream this repository would write or any stream a conforming implementation would. It is reachable from a NON-conforming stream, which is exactly why the decoder must say something honest about it.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.implemented_as: klv_codec.decode_ber_length raises UnderivableFromPinnedCopy carrying park 8 and ST 0107.3-03. Fixture length_indefinite_first_octet, whose generator check asserts the exception TYPE so a later round cannot decide what 0x80 means without buying the document.

underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.rule: Any ceiling on the NUMBER of length octets.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.status: NOT STATED BY ST 0107.3. PARK 8, and recorded as an absence that was searched for rather than one that was assumed.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.what_the_pinned_copy_does_say: SS 6.3.2 states no maximum. The document's only maxima are elsewhere and govern a different quantity: SS 6.3.3 'items may have maximum lengths defined. When encoding a Value do not exceed the maximum limits', and ST 0107.3-07, 'Where a MISB standard defines a numeric maximum Length for a Local Set item's Value, the encoded Value shall not exceed the number of bytes defined by the maximum Length'. Both bound a VALUE's size, not a length field's width. The whole six pages were searched for 'maximum', 'limit', 'ceiling' and the numerals 127 and 128; the only occurrences are those two and SS 6.3.2's own 'values less than 128'.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.the_bound_the_codec_uses_is_STRUCTURAL_a: BER_LENGTH_OF_LENGTH_MAX = 127, because the first octet carries the long-form flag in bit 7 and the count in the remaining seven bits, so 127 is the largest count that octet can express. That is arithmetic on the shape SS 6.3.2's own examples fix, not a citation, and the constant's comment says so. Whether ST 336 imposes a LOWER ceiling is park 8's.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.implemented_as: encode_ber_length raises UnderivableFromPinnedCopy above the structural bound, carrying park 8 and the sentence that states no ceiling. Not KLVFramingError: a caller asking for a 128-octet length field is not handing over wrong bytes, they are asking a question this repository cannot answer.

underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.rule: Whether a DECODER must reject a non-minimal length.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.status: UNDERIVABLE AS A NORM, DECIDED AS AN IMPLEMENTATION - and the decision now rests on live authority, which is the difference from the framing round's version of this same entry.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.what_the_pinned_copy_does_say: ST 0107.3-05 is a 'shall' on the ENCODING: lengths 'shall be BER Short form or BER Long form encoded using the fewest possible bytes'. It does not say what a reader does when it meets a violation. SS 6.3.2's prose frames the two non-minimal forms as inefficient - 'BER becomes less efficient' - rather than as invalid, which pulls gently the other way.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.the_decision: klv_codec.decode_ber_length REFUSES both, as KLVFramingError - these bytes are wrong - because ST 0107.3-05 says they are wrong, in the live edition ST 0601.14a's live route points at. The second reason is the one the framing round gave for tags: accepting them would make several byte strings denote one length, and a round trip over an ambiguous encoding is a statement about the codec rather than about the wire.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.the_sentence_that_pulls_the_other_way_an: ST 0107.3-04 requires decoders to 'skip unknown Local Set values so as to not impact the decoding of known Local Set items', which is a be-permissive requirement. It is about unknown TAGS, not malformed lengths, and a decoder cannot honour it at all without first reading the length correctly - so a strict length reader is compatible with it. Recorded because the tension is real and an unstated tension reads as an unexamined one.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.what_is_not_claimed: That refusal is normatively required of a decoder. If a later ST 0107 or ST 336 requires acceptance, this is the decision that changes - and it is the same sentence the framing round wrote about the tag refusal, which is now discharged. This one is not.

park_4.document: MISB ST 0107.3, KLV Metadata in Motion Imagery
park_4.what_discharged_it: BOTH halves of parks.shared_exit_condition, and it needed both. FIRST HALF: the exact version the delegation table pins was obtained - 0107.3, not the current 0107.4 - and pinned in fixtures/klv/spec/ by SHA-256, byte count and page count with its title-page identity read, at delegated_specifications_held.st_0107_3. SECOND HALF: 'the row set that document supports' is written. ST 0107.3 defines no tag table and has no row set to write; what it supports is the FRAMING GRAMMAR, and that is klv_codec.decode_ber_length, encode_ber_length and walk_local_set, which stopped raising this round, plus thirteen new fixtures in fixtures/klv/framing/.
park_4.why_the_second_half_was_not_waived_and_h: Because park 1 was not given that discount and park 2 is still open for exactly this reason - ST 0102.12 has been held since 2026-08-26 and its park stays open on the stated ground that no row set is written from it. So 'the row set that document supports' had to be read for a document that supports no rows. It is read as 'the artefact this document makes writable', which for a field dictionary is a row set and for a framing standard is a codec. A park closed on the document alone would have been the same table treated two ways; a park held open for a row set the document cannot support would have been the same table treated two ways in the other direction.
park_4.what_it_does_not_discharge: Any other park, and in particular not the ones the ST 0601 rows are still blocked on: 8 owns what remains of the encoding, 3 owns the epoch, 5 owns the IMAPB ranges. Closing park 4 moved this adapter from 'can name every field and read none' to 'can find every item and decode no value'. The 141 tag rows still say 'not yet' and none of them was eligible to move: a framing rule says where an item begins, never what it means.

park_8.document: SMPTE ST 336:2017, Data Encoding Protocol Using Key-Length-Value
park_8.what_this_round_established_about_it: The precise size of what it owns, narrowed for the second time in one day. The framing round left it owning 'the LENGTH grammar and the third BER-OID octet'. ST 0107.3 states both. WHAT IS LEFT IS TWO THINGS AND BOTH ARE ABSENCES: 0x80 as a first length octet, which ST 0107.3 never mentions, and any ceiling on the count of length octets, which ST 0107.3 does not state. Neither is reachable from a conforming stream, which is why the codec is complete with the park open.
park_8.why_it_does_not_close: It is a purchase decision, the document is not held, and a narrower park is still an open park. Recording that a blocker shrank is not recording that it lifted - the same sentence the framing round wrote, and it is still the right one.
park_8.what_did_change_and_it_is_not_a_closure: A THIRD held document now pins ST 336:2017. ST 0107.3's reference [1] reads 'SMPTE ST 336:2017 Data Encoding Protocol Using Key-Length-Value', matching ST 0601.14a's ref [2] and MISP-2019.1's Appendix B ref [13] exactly. ST 0102.12's ref [3] still pins ST 336:2007. So the divergence registered as KLV 11 is now three documents against one rather than two against one, which strengthens the majority and does not resolve the question - see the KLV 11 update.
park_8.the_economics_moved_and_it_is_recorded_n: ST 0107.3 SS 6.3.3.1 names a DIFFERENT source for the length grammar than the parks table does: 'Items using "ber" types in the MISB standards use the ASN.1 [4] Basic Encoding Rules for Lengths rules', where [4] is 'ITU Rec X.680 (08/15)'. ITU recommendations are free downloads. If the BER rules the residue needs are obtainable from ITU rather than from SMPTE, park 8's 'somebody has to spend money' framing is wrong for part of what it owns. NOT ACTED ON, for two reasons: BER's encoding rules are X.690 and not X.680, so the reference itself needs adjudicating (registered as KLV 13), and changing a park's reopen route on the strength of a reference list read in passing is the roster change the park 1 round refused to make.

the_park_outcome.no_row_flipped: All 141 rows of tag_table_st_0601_14 remain 'not yet' and none was eligible to move. The round predicted no flips and there were none - the same prediction and the same outcome as the framing round, for the same reason.
the_park_outcome.no_park_opened_and_none_renumbered: The roster is unchanged at twelve parks. Two are now closed - park 1 by the tag-table round and park 4 by this one - and ten remain open, nine of them public downloads and one a purchase.

what_was_implemented_and_what_deliberate.four_of_the_new_fixtures_are_the_documen: 0x02, 0x8180, 0x8102 and 0x8300 0080 are the four encodings SS 6.3.2 prints while explaining which two are wasteful. what_was_implemented_and_what_deliberate.bidirectionality: Claimed for what exists and checked by exhaustion where the domain permits, which for lengths it does not. decode_ber_length(encode_ber_length(n)) == n exhaustively over 0..131071 and by boundary vector at every octet-width transition out to 2**500; decode_ber_oid(encode_ber_oid(n)) == n exhaustively over 0..16383 and by boundary vector either side of each 7-bit transition out to five octets. The exhaustive ranges are the ones that fit in a test.
what_was_implemented_and_what_deliberate.no_klv_payload_fixture_yet_and_the_reaso: fixtures/klv/ still holds no .klv adapter fixture, and the reason is no longer the length grammar. what_was_implemented_and_what_deliberate.no_tag_semantics_no_fusion_no_joins: Values are opaque octets throughout. walk_local_set yields tags and bytes; nothing knows what tag 2 means and nothing joins two items.
